# Brazilian Music (Música Brasileira)

> +160 genres and subgenres, +2,500 music artists, +1,700 songs and +350 albums: Brazilian music catalogued in English and Portuguese.

Brazilian Music (Música Brasileira) is a free, bilingual catalogue of Brazilian music, part of BiblioVerse. English lives at the root and Brazilian Portuguese at /pt/. Every artist, person, subgenre, award, festival and TV show has its own page with links to Wikipedia, Spotify, Last.fm and YouTube. Artists are ranked in three tiers: S (legend), A (giant) and B (reference). Song and album credits name the performers, not the composers. Last updated: 2026-11-14.

## Genres and subgenres

### [Samba](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/samba.html) (since 1860)

Heir to the samba de roda of Bahia's Recôncavo, carried into the homes of Rio's 'Bahian aunts' in the early 20th century, samba is the rhythm the world associates with Brazil. 'Pelo Telefone' (1917) is the first registered samba; from there came the samba schools, samba-canção, partido-alto and, in the 1980s, pagode. Where: Rio de Janeiro.

- [Samba de roda](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/samba-de-roda.html) (since 1860; UNESCO intangible heritage · 2005): The samba of Bahia's Recôncavo, with handclaps, plate-and-knife and viola machete; the root of Rio samba. Dona Edith do Prato, Mariene de Castro.
- [Roots samba](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/samba-raiz.html) (since 1917; Brazilian heritage · IPHAN 2007): The samba of the hills and the schools: Cartola, Nelson Cavaquinho, Paulinho da Viola.
- [Samba-canção](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/samba-cancao.html) (since 1930): Slow, romantic samba of the radio era, from Noel Rosa and Ary Barroso to Dolores Duran.
- [Samba de breque](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/samba-de-breque.html) (since 1935): Samba with stops ('breques') where the singer speaks a comic tale; Moreira da Silva is the master, Germano Mathias the heir.
- [Samba-exaltação](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/samba-exaltacao.html) (since 1939): Grand orchestral samba that praises the country; 'Aquarela do Brasil' (Ary Barroso, 1939) is the landmark.
- [Samba-enredo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/samba-enredo.html) (since 1930; Brazilian heritage · IPHAN 2007): The samba that tells each school's parade theme at Rio carnival.
- [Partido-alto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/partido-alto.html) (since 1920; Brazilian heritage · IPHAN 2007): Improvised circle samba, with a collective chorus and verses made up on the spot.
- [Samba-jazz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/samba-jazz.html) (since 1958; Fusion genre: samba + jazz (bebop)): 1960s instrumental trios (Tamba Trio, Zimbo Trio, Edison Machado) mixing samba and bebop.
- [Afro-samba](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/afro-samba.html) (since 1966; Fusion genre: samba + Afro-Bahian candomblé chants): Baden Powell and Vinicius de Moraes brought the chants and rhythms of Bahian candomblé into samba on the album Os Afro-sambas (1966), with Quarteto em Cy: 'Canto de Ossanha', 'Berimbau'.
- [Sambalanço](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/sambalanco.html) (since 1958; Fusion genre: samba + jazz): The danceable nightclub samba of the 1960s, between samba and jazz: Orlandivo, Ed Lincoln, Miltinho, Wilson Simonal.
- [Samba de gafieira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/samba-de-gafieira.html) (since 1940): The instrumental samba of the dance halls, with horns: Severino Araújo and the Orquestra Tabajara, Paulo Moura.
- [Samba-rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/samba-rock.html) (since 1963; Fusion genre: samba + rock, soul and funk): The swing of Jorge Ben Jor and São Paulo's black dance halls; it has its own ballroom dance.
- [Pagode](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/pagode.html) (since 1980): Born at Cacique de Ramos with Fundo de Quintal: banjo, tantã and hand repique.
- [Romantic pagode](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/pagode-romantico.html) (since 1990): The São Paulo strand of the 1990s (Raça Negra, Só Pra Contrariar, Exaltasamba), today led by Thiaguinho and Ferrugem.

### [Choro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/choro.html) (since 1770)

Brazil's first urban instrumental genre: European polkas and waltzes played with African syncopation on flute, cavaquinho and guitars. Pixinguinha is the central name; 'Carinhoso' and 'Brasileirinho' are known worldwide. Where: Rio de Janeiro.

- [Modinha and lundu](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/modinha-lundu.html) (since 1770): The 18th-century parlour song and Afro-Brazilian dance that came before choro and samba; Xisto Bahia and Catulo da Paixão Cearense.
- [Maxixe](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/maxixe.html) (since 1875): The 'excommunicated' dance of late 19th-century Rio, mixing polka and lundu; Chiquinha Gonzaga and Ernesto Nazareth.
- [Choro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/choro.html) (since 1870; Brazilian heritage · IPHAN 2024): Choro circles still happen in bars and squares; the seven-string guitar plays the bass runs.

### [Bossa Nova](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/bossa.html) (since 1958)

Slowed-down samba, jazz harmony and a near-whispered voice: bossa nova was born in Rio's Zona Sul apartments with João Gilberto, Tom Jobim and Vinicius de Moraes, and in 1964 'The Girl from Ipanema' made it the most-heard Brazilian music on the planet. Where: Rio de Janeiro.

- [Bossa nova](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/bossa-nova.html) (since 1958): The 1958–64 generation and its heirs (Bebel Gilberto, Celso Fonseca).

### [MPB](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/mpb.html) (since 1965)

'Música Popular Brasileira' is the name the country gave, from the 1960s TV festivals on, to the sophisticated songwriting of Chico Buarque, Elis Regina, Caetano Veloso, Gilberto Gil, Milton Nascimento and Djavan. It is not a rhythm: it is a song tradition that absorbs samba, bossa, baião, rock and jazz. Where: TV festivals, Rio and São Paulo.

- [Festival-era MPB](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/mpb-classica.html) (since 1965): The generation of Elis, Chico, Edu Lobo and Milton, forged at the Record and Globo festivals under the dictatorship.
- [Tropicália](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/tropicalia.html) (since 1967): Caetano, Gil, Gal, Tom Zé and Os Mutantes mixed electric guitars, bossa and avant-garde; it lasted two years and changed everything.
- [Clube da Esquina](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/clube-da-esquina.html) (since 1972): Milton Nascimento, Lô Borges, Beto Guedes and Toninho Horta: Minas harmony, Beatles and jazz.
- [Pessoal do Ceará](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/pessoal-do-ceara.html) (since 1972): Belchior, Fagner and Ednardo brought the urban Northeast into 1970s song.
- [New MPB](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/nova-mpb.html) (since 1990): From Marisa Monte and Lenine to Tim Bernardes, Liniker and Marina Sena: 21st-century Brazilian song.
- [Vanguarda Paulista](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/vanguarda-paulista.html) (since 1979): Itamar Assumpção, Arrigo Barnabé, Grupo Rumo and Premeditando o Breque at the Lira Paulistana theatre: experimental, independent song.
- [Armorial music](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/armorial.html) (since 1970; Fusion genre: concert music + Northeastern folk culture): Northeastern-rooted concert music conceived by Ariano Suassuna: Quinteto Armorial and Antonio Nóbrega.

### [Brazilian Rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/rock.html) (since 1955)

It began with rock'n'roll covers in 1955, became Jovem Guarda in the 1960s, psychedelia with Os Mutantes, and exploded in the 1980s with the 'BRock' of Legião Urbana, Titãs and Paralamas. It has export-grade metal (Sepultura, Angra), hardcore, manguebeat, emo and a vigorous indie scene. Where: Rio, São Paulo, Brasília and the whole country.

- [Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/jovem-guarda.html) (since 1965): The youth rock of TV Record with Roberto Carlos, Erasmo Carlos and Wanderléa.
- [Psychedelic rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/psicodelico.html) (since 1966): From Os Mutantes and Raul Seixas to Boogarins: Brazilian psychedelia never stopped.
- [Progressive rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/progressivo.html) (since 1970): O Terço, Som Imaginário, Casa das Máquinas and Bacamarte in the 1970s.
- [Rock rural](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/rock-rural.html) (since 1972; Fusion genre: rock + folk + caipira music): Sá, Rodrix & Guarabyra mixed rock, folk and viola caipira; Zé Geraldo followed the road.
- [Hard rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/hard-rock.html) (since 1967): Made in Brazil, Patrulha do Espaço, Dr. Sin and the new wave of English-singing bands.
- [BRock (1980s)](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/brock.html) (since 1982): The Rock in Rio 1985 generation: Legião, Titãs, Paralamas, Barão, Capital, RPM, Kid Abelha, Blitz, Ultraje.
- [Post-punk / new wave](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/pos-punk.html) (since 1981): Blitz, Ira!, Plebe Rude, Metrô and Zero; the sound of Brasília and São Paulo in the early 1980s.
- [Brasília rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/rock-brasilia.html) (since 1978): The capital produced Aborto Elétrico, Legião Urbana, Capital Inicial, Plebe Rude, Raimundos and Scalene.
- [Gaúcho rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/rock-gaucho.html) (since 1983): Engenheiros do Hawaii, Nenhum de Nós, Os Replicantes, Cachorro Grande and Fresno: the 'gaúcho invasion'.
- [Punk](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/punk.html) (since 1979): Cólera, Inocentes, Garotos Podres and Ratos de Porão; São Paulo was the capital of Latin American punk.
- [Heavy and power metal](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/heavy-power.html) (since 1982): Stress, Viper, Angra, Shaman and Hibria: Brazilian melodic metal, with Andre Matos as its emblematic voice.
- [Thrash, death and black metal](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/thrash-death.html) (since 1981): Vulcano, Sepultura, Sarcófago, Korzus, Krisiun, Nervosa and Crypta; Belo Horizonte and São Paulo are capitals of extreme metal.
- [Manguebeat](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/manguebeat.html) (since 1991; Fusion genre: maracatu + rock + hip-hop): Recife, 1990s: maracatu, rock and hip-hop with Chico Science & Nação Zumbi and Mundo Livre S/A.
- [Rap rock / nu metal](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/rap-rock.html) (since 1993; Fusion genre: rap + rock): Planet Hemp, O Rappa, Charlie Brown Jr. and Tihuana ruled the 1990s–2000s.
- [Fock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/fock.html) (since 1998; Fusion genre: rock + funk carioca): Rock and metal with the beat and vocal style of funk carioca, sometimes with rap. The mix began in Porto Alegre in the late 1990s with Comunidade Nin-Jitsu ('Detetive', from the album Broncas Legais, 1998), DeFalla and Ultramen. In the 2020s it got a name: fock, as MC Taya called it, and metal mandrake, the movement of the new heavy scene. Lvcas turns funk hits into metal.
- [Hardcore](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/hardcore.html) (since 1991): Dead Fish, CPM 22, Garage Fuzz and Sugar Kane; the Deckdisc and Hearts Bleed Blue labels.
- [Emo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/emo.html) (since 1996): Fresno, NX Zero, Hateen and Dance of Days; Brazilian emo had its own mainstream in 2006–2010.
- [Pop punk](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/pop-punk.html) (since 2003): Strike, Restart, Fake Number; the colourful 'happy rock' of the late 2000s.
- [Post-hardcore / metalcore](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/metalcore.html) (since 2002): Gloria, Menores Atos, Bullet Bane, Project46.
- [Indie rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/indie.html) (since 1997): Los Hermanos opened the door; then O Terno, Terno Rei, Boogarins, Vanguart, Maglore and Jovem Dionisio.
- [Alternative rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/rock-alternativo.html) (since 1990): Pitty, Detonautas, Scalene, Supercombo, Far From Alaska.
- [Stoner rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/stoner.html) (since 2004): Goiás is the epicentre (Black Drawing Chalks, Dry, Hellbenders); dozens of bands across the country.
- [Grunge / post-grunge](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/grunge.html) (since 1994): O Surto, Reação em Cadeia, Malta, Ego Kill Talent.
- [Shoegaze](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/shoegaze.html) (since 2008): A fertile 2010s scene: Terno Rei, Loomer, Lupe de Lupe, Gorduratrans and dozens of projects.
- [Garage rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/garage.html) (since 1965): From Os Baobás to Autoramas and Cachorro Grande; today Karen Dió and Violet Soda.
- [Ska / reggae rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/ska.html) (since 1982; Fusion genre: rock + ska + reggae): Paralamas, Skank and Forfun in the mainstream; an independent ska scene in several cities.
- [Pop rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/pop-rock.html) (since 1974): Lulu Santos, Roupa Nova, Kid Abelha, Skank, Jota Quest, Lagum: the rock that plays on the radio.
- [Comic rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/rock-comico.html) (since 1980): Ultraje a Rigor, Mamonas Assassinas, Velhas Virgens, Massacration, Pedra Letícia: humour is a tradition in Brazilian rock.
- [Christian rock](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/rock-cristao.html) (since 1987): Oficina G3, Rosa de Saron, Resgate and Catedral.

### [Sertanejo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/sertanejo.html) (since 1929)

Brazil's most-streamed genre today was born as caipira music in 1929, with viola duos singing in thirds. It modernized with Chitãozinho & Xororó, became romantic pop in the 1990s and, after 2005, the 'universitário' of Jorge & Mateus, Luan Santana and Marília Mendonça took over the charts. Where: Rural São Paulo, Minas, Goiás and Paraná.

- [Caipira / roots](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/caipira.html) (since 1929): Viola caipira, duos in thirds and rural themes: Tonico & Tinoco, Tião Carreiro & Pardinho, Inezita Barroso, Almir Sater.
- [Romantic sertanejo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/sertanejo-romantico.html) (since 1982): Heartbreak ballads with Chitãozinho & Xororó, Leandro & Leonardo, Zezé Di Camargo & Luciano and Bruno & Marrone.
- [Sertanejo universitário](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/universitario.html) (since 2005): Born at student parties in Goiânia and Londrina: Jorge & Mateus, Luan Santana, Gusttavo Lima, Michel Teló, Henrique & Juliano.
- [Feminejo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/feminejo.html) (since 2015): The genre's female turn with Marília Mendonça, Maiara & Maraisa, Simone & Simaria and Lauana Prado.
- [Forronejo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/forronejo.html) (since 2001; Fusion genre: forró + sertanejo): Forró and sertanejo on the same groove. Osmar & Osmailson took it nationwide in 2001; Wesley Safadão made it massive from 2015 on.
- [Funknejo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/funknejo.html) (since 2012; Fusion genre: funk carioca + sertanejo): Funk carioca beats such as tamborzão with the melodies and duos of sertanejo universitário: João Lucas & Marcelo, Cácio & Marcos, Dennis DJ.
- [Pagonejo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/pagonejo.html) (since 2018; Fusion genre: pagode + sertanejo): Pagode meets sertanejo: 'Atrasadinha' (2018), by Felipe Araújo and Ferrugem, topped the charts; Alexandre Pires released the album Pagonejo Bão (2025).
- [Rocknejo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/rocknejo.html) (since 2009; Fusion genre: rock + sertanejo): Sertanejo with distorted guitars and rock drums. By 2009 Hardneja Sertacore was already playing sertanejo hits as hardcore; the name rocknejo spread with the Rocknejo carnival bloc, founded in Belo Horizonte in 2018, and with party bands. Edson & Hudson and Lauana Prado are examples of the mix too.
- [Agronejo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/agronejo.html) (since 2021): Sertanejo with funk and agribusiness aesthetics: Ana Castela, Luan Pereira, Zé Felipe.

### [Brazilian Funk](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/funk.html) (since 1989)

Nothing to do with American funk: funk carioca was born at 1980s dance parties out of Miami bass and found its Portuguese voice with DJ Marlboro (1989). It moved through melody, proibidão, tamborzão, São Paulo's ostentação and 150 BPM; today 'baile funk' is exported by Anitta, Kevin o Chris and São Paulo's mandelão. Where: Rio de Janeiro, then São Paulo.

- [Funk melody](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/funk-melody.html) (since 1994): Romantic and sung: MC Marcinho, Claudinho & Buchecha, Latino.
- [Conscious funk](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/funk-consciente.html) (since 1995): Lyrics about favela life: 'Rap da Felicidade', 'Rap do Silva', MC Carol.
- [Proibidão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/proibidao.html) (since 1995): Explicit or crime-linked funk, circulating outside radio; Mr. Catra and Tati Quebra Barraco broke the barrier.
- [Tamborzão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/tamborzao.html) (since 1998): The Afro-Brazilian percussion beat built by DJ Luciano Oliveira in the late 1990s became the sound of 2000s funk carioca: Bonde do Tigrão, Tati Quebra Barraco, Mr. Catra.
- [Funk ostentação](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/ostentacao.html) (since 2011): São Paulo, 2011–14: cars, brands and champagne with MC Guimê, MC Daleste and MC Livinho.
- [150 BPM funk](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/funk-150.html) (since 2014): Rennan da Penha and Baile da Gaiola sped up funk carioca; Kevin o Chris is the main name.
- [Rasteirinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/rasteirinha.html) (since 2012): Slower funk with a reggaeton and dancehall sway, born in Rio's favelas in the early 2010s; MC WM's 'Fuleragem' is its anthem.
- [Mandelão / bruxaria](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/mandelao.html) (since 2019): São Paulo funk of the 2020s: distorted bass, 'automotivo', DJs such as Arana and Ws da Igrejinha, MCs such as Ryan SP and IG.
- [Brega funk](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/brega-funk.html) (since 2016; Fusion genre: brega + funk): Recife mixed brega and funk; 'Envolvimento' (MC Loma, 2018) became a national craze.
- [Funk pop](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/funk-pop.html) (since 2013; Fusion genre: funk + pop): Funk on global charts: Anitta, Ludmilla, Pedro Sampaio, Dennis DJ, Kevinho.

### [Rap and Hip-Hop](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/rap.html) (since 1988)

Brazilian hip-hop grew up in black dance parties and at São Paulo's São Bento metro station. Racionais MC's gave the genre its masterpiece in 1997; in the 2010s Emicida, Criolo and Djonga took rap to the centre of culture, and Matuê made trap the most-streamed sound among the young. Where: São Paulo, then Rio, Brasília and Fortaleza.

- [Rap nacional](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/rap-nacional.html) (since 1988): From Thaíde & DJ Hum and Racionais to Emicida, Criolo, Djonga and BK': chronicles of the periphery.
- [Brazilian trap](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/trap.html) (since 2016): Matuê and 30PRAUM (Teto, Wiu), Veigh, L7nnon, Orochi: hi-hats and autotune in Portuguese.
- [Drill](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/drill.html) (since 2019): The sliding beats of Chicago and London drill in Portuguese: Vandal in Bahia, Leall and L7nnon in Rio.
- [Slam and spoken word](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/slam.html) (since 2008): Spoken poetry as a competition, born from hip-hop: in 2008 Roberta Estrela D'Alva founded ZAP! (Zona Autônoma da Palavra) in São Paulo, Brazil's first slam. Since 2014 SLAM BR has brought together poets from across the country and sends its winner to the Slam World Cup in Paris. Mel Duarte.

### [Forró](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/forro.html) (since 1946)

Luiz Gonzaga invented the accordion, zabumba and triangle trio and launched baião in 1946; 'Asa Branca' is the anthem of the sertão. From xote and xaxado to pé-de-serra, forró reached the universities in the 1990s, the huge stages of Fortaleza's electronic forró and, in the 2020s, piseiro. Where: Pernambuco, Paraíba, Ceará and the whole Northeast.

- [Baião](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/baiao.html) (since 1946; Brazilian heritage · IPHAN 2021): The rhythm Gonzaga took to national radio; it influenced everyone from Hermeto Pascoal to Raul Seixas.
- [Xote and xaxado](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/xote-xaxado.html) (since 1949; Brazilian heritage · IPHAN 2021): Ballroom xote and the xaxado of the cangaceiros, taken to record by Luiz Gonzaga and Marinês.
- [Pé-de-serra forró](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/forro-pe-de-serra.html) (since 1950; Brazilian heritage · IPHAN 2021): Xote, baião and arrasta-pé with the traditional trio: Dominguinhos, Trio Nordestino, Falamansa.
- [Forró universitário](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/forro-universitario.html) (since 1998): Pé-de-serra rediscovered by São Paulo's young people in the late 1990s: Falamansa, Rastapé, Bicho de Pé.
- [Electronic forró](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/forro-eletronico.html) (since 1990): Fortaleza, 1990s: keyboards, horns and huge stage bands (Mastruz com Leite, Aviões do Forró, Wesley Safadão).
- [Piseiro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/piseiro.html) (since 2019): Sped-up forró with the 'pisadinha' keyboard: Barões da Pisadinha, João Gomes, Zé Vaqueiro.

### [Axé and Bahian Music](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/axe.html) (since 1949)

Salvador invented the trio elétrico in 1950 and, in 1985, Luiz Caldas's 'Fricote' christened axé: Bahian frevo, ijexá, reggae and pop. Olodum created samba-reggae; Daniela Mercury and Ivete Sangalo took it nationwide. Salvador's carnival is the genre's biggest stage. Where: Salvador, Bahia.

- [Trio elétrico](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/trio-eletrico.html) (since 1950): Dodô & Osmar put electric guitars on top of a 1929 Ford; modern Salvador carnival was born.
- [Afoxé and ijexá](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/afoxe-ijexa.html) (since 1949): Afoxé processions to the ijexá, a candomblé rhythm; Filhos de Gandhy have paraded at Salvador carnival since 1949.
- [Axé music](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/axe-music.html) (since 1985): Luiz Caldas, Chiclete com Banana, Daniela Mercury, Ivete Sangalo, Claudia Leitte.
- [Samba-reggae and afro blocos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/samba-reggae.html) (since 1986; Fusion genre: samba + reggae): Olodum, Ilê Aiyê, Timbalada and Carlinhos Brown: Afro-Bahian percussion of Black affirmation.
- [Pagode baiano](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/pagode-baiano.html) (since 1992): Choreographies and spicy lyrics: É o Tchan, Harmonia do Samba, Psirico, Léo Santana.
- [Pagofunk](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/pagofunk.html) (since 2006; Fusion genre: pagode baiano + funk carioca): A branch of pagode baiano with funk carioca elements, created in Salvador in 2006 by Robyssão, then with the band Black Style; the soundtrack of the outskirts' street sound systems.
- [Arrocha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/arrocha.html) (since 2000): Romantic ballads danced 'tight' in rural Bahia: Pablo, Tierry.
- [Arrochadeira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/arrochadeira.html) (since 2000; Fusion genre: arrocha + pagode baiano): Also called bregadeira: arrocha with the electronic percussion of pagode baiano, born in Bahia in the 2000s. Vingadora's 'Paredão Metralhadora' took it nationwide.

### [Brazilian Pop](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/pop.html) (since 1976)

From disco-era girl groups (Frenéticas) to the teen pop of Sandy & Junior and Rouge, to the global divas of the 21st century: Anitta, Pabllo Vittar, Ludmilla, Iza and Luísa Sonza. Today's Brazilian pop absorbs funk, sertanejo and R&B and leads the streaming platforms. Where: São Paulo and Rio.

- [Contemporary pop](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/pop-contemporaneo.html) (since 1985): Radio and streaming pop singers: from Rosana and Wanessa Camargo to Anitta, Iza, Luísa Sonza and Pabllo Vittar.
- [Disco and dance-pop](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/disco-dance.html) (since 1976): The disco craze with Frenéticas, Harmony Cats, Gretchen, Lady Zu and Sidney Magal.
- [Teen pop](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/teen-pop.html) (since 1989): Sandy & Junior, Kelly Key, Rouge, KLB, Dominó and the idols of teen soap operas.
- [Alternative pop](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/pop-alternativo.html) (since 2016): Jão, Marina Sena, Duda Beat, Tiago Iorc, Melim: platform-era songwriting pop.
- [LGBTQIA+ pop](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/pop-lgbt.html) (since 2016): Pabllo Vittar, Gloria Groove, Linn da Quebrada, Urias: drag and dissidence at the top of the charts.

### [Brega, Calypso and Sounds of Pará](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/brega.html) (since 1800)

'Brega' was a critics' insult for the popular romantic music of Waldick Soriano, Odair José and Reginaldo Rossi; it became a genre name. In Pará, brega met carimbó and guitarrada and produced lambada, Banda Calypso and the tecnobrega of Belém's giant sound systems. Where: Recife, Belém and inland Brazil.

- [Romantic brega](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/brega-romantico.html) (since 1960): Reginaldo Rossi, Waldick Soriano, Odair José, Wando, Amado Batista.
- [Pernambuco brega](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/brega-pernambucano.html) (since 1990): The brega of Recife's dance bands: Conde Só Brega, Michelle Melo, Priscila Senna; the father of brega funk.
- [Carimbó](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/carimbo.html) (since 1800): Dance and rhythm from Pará, with curimbó drums; Pinduca and Dona Onete.
- [Guitarrada](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/guitarrada.html) (since 1978; Fusion genre: carimbó + cumbia + surf music): Instrumental guitar music from Pará created by Mestre Vieira: carimbó, cumbia and surf music.
- [Lambada](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/lambada.html) (since 1976; Fusion genre: carimbó + guitarrada + cumbia + merengue): From Pará and Bahia to the world in 1989 (Kaoma); Beto Barbosa is the king.
- [Lambadão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/lambadao.html) (since 1999; Fusion genre: lambada + siriri + rasqueado): The sped-up lambada of the Cuiabá lowlands: in Poconé (Mato Grosso), musicians mixed lambada, carimbó, siriri and rasqueado. Estrela Dalva, Os Maninhos, Chico Gil.
- [Pará calypso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/calypso.html) (since 1999): Joelma and Chimbinha's Banda Calypso sold millions without a label.
- [Tecnobrega](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/tecnobrega.html) (since 2002; Fusion genre: brega + electronic music): Home-made electronic production and giant sound systems in Belém; Gaby Amarantos, Gang do Eletro.

### [Gospel and Religious Music](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/gospel.html) (since 1966)

One of Brazil's biggest music markets: the evangelical worship of Aline Barros, Fernandinho, Gabriela Rocha and Diante do Trono fills stadiums and leads YouTube, while Padre Marcelo Rossi's Catholic music sold millions in the 1990s. There is also Christian rock, rap and sertanejo. Where: The whole country.

- [Worship](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/louvor.html) (since 1998): Diante do Trono, Aline Barros, Fernandinho, Gabriela Rocha, Isadora Pompeo.
- [Pentecostal gospel](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/gospel-pentecostal.html) (since 1980): Cassiane, Damares, Bruna Karla: the tradition of Pentecostal churches.
- [Catholic music](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/musica-catolica.html) (since 1966): Padre Zezinho, Padre Marcelo Rossi, Padre Fábio de Melo.
- [Gospel rap](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/rap-gospel.html) (since 1998; Fusion genre: rap + gospel): Pregador Luo and Ao Cubo.

### [Electronic](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/eletronica.html) (since 1995)

DJ Marky took Brazilian drum'n'bass to London in the 1990s; in the 2010s, the 'Brazilian bass' of Alok and Vintage Culture placed Brazilian DJs among the world's most streamed. The country has one of the largest psytrance scenes and a constant dialogue between electronics and funk. Where: São Paulo, Goiânia and festivals nationwide.

- [Brazilian bass](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/brazilian-bass.html) (since 2014): Deep house with heavy bass lines: Alok, Vintage Culture, KVSH, Bhaskar, Cat Dealers.
- [Brazilian drum'n'bass](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/dnb-brasileiro.html) (since 1995; Fusion genre: drum'n'bass + samba): DJ Marky, Patife and XRS; 'LK' (2002) and 'Sambassim' crossed samba and jungle.
- [House and techno](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/house-techno.html) (since 2000): Gui Boratto on Kompakt, ANNA and Mochakk on the world's dancefloors: Brazil in house and techno.
- [Psytrance](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/psytrance.html) (since 1998): Festivals such as Universo Paralello (BA) make Brazil a psychedelic-trance powerhouse.
- [Electronics and funk](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/electro-funk.html) (since 2003; Fusion genre: funk carioca + electronic music): CSS, Bonde do Rolê, Tropkillaz, Omulu and Pedro Sampaio: baile funk in the club.

### [Brazilian Reggae](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/reggae.html) (since 1975)

São Luís do Maranhão is the 'Brazilian Jamaica', where roots reggae has played on sound systems since the 1970s. In the 1990s Cidade Negra and, later, Natiruts, Armandinho and Maneva made Portuguese-language reggae a mass genre. Where: São Luís, Rio, Brasília and Bahia.

- [National reggae](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/reggae-brasileiro.html) (since 1986): Cidade Negra, Natiruts, Armandinho, Maneva, Planta & Raiz, Edson Gomes.
- [Maranhão reggae](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/reggae-maranhense.html) (since 1975): Sound systems, close-dancing 'agarradinho' and Tribo de Jah in São Luís.

### [Soul and Black Music](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/soul.html) (since 1969)

Tim Maia came back from the United States in 1970 and invented Brazilian soul; the Black Rio movement's dance parties, Banda Black Rio, Toni Tornado and Jorge Ben created a funk-soul with its own identity. Today Liniker, Iza and Ed Motta carry the lineage. Where: Rio and São Paulo.

- [Brazilian soul](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/soul-brasileiro.html) (since 1970): Tim Maia, Cassiano, Hyldon, Sandra de Sá, Ed Motta.
- [Samba-soul](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/samba-soul.html) (since 1970; Fusion genre: samba + soul): Samba with the swing and the singing of soul: Jorge Ben Jor, Wilson Simonal, Seu Jorge.
- [Samba-funk](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/samba-funk.html) (since 1969; Fusion genre: samba + American funk): Samba with the American funk of James Brown and Kool & the Gang: keyboards, wah-wah guitar and a heavy bass. Created in 1969 by pianist Dom Salvador and Grupo Abolição, which gave rise to Banda Black Rio; Tim Maia and Jorge Ben Jor dipped into it too.
- [Black Rio](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/black-rio.html) (since 1976): Funk and soul dance parties in Rio's North Zone in the 1970s; Banda Black Rio, Toni Tornado, Gerson King Combo.
- [Neo-soul and R&B](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/neo-soul.html) (since 2015): Liniker, Iza, Luccas Carlos, Tássia Reis, Paula Lima.

### [Jazz and Instrumental](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/instrumental.html) (since 1930)

Hermeto Pascoal, Egberto Gismonti, Airto Moreira and Naná Vasconcelos are revered by world jazz; Azymuth became a DJ cult; Toninho Horta and Hamilton de Holanda take Brazilian guitar and mandolin to international stages. Where: Rio, São Paulo, Minas and Pernambuco.

- [Brazilian jazz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/jazz-brasileiro.html) (since 1960): Hermeto, Egberto, Moacir Santos, Quarteto Novo, Hamilton de Holanda, André Mehmari.
- [Fusion and jazz-funk](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/fusion-brasileira.html) (since 1973; Fusion genre: jazz + funk + Brazilian music): Azymuth, Eumir Deodato, Cama de Gato: the rediscovered Brazilian groove of the 1970s.
- [Brazilian guitar](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/violao-brasileiro.html) (since 1930): The school of Brazilian solo guitar: Garoto, Dilermando Reis, Baden Powell, Raphael Rabello, Yamandu Costa.

### [Classical Music](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/classica.html) (since 1760)

Carlos Gomes premiered 'O Guarani' at La Scala in 1870; Heitor Villa-Lobos made the 'Bachianas Brasileiras' the most-performed Brazilian classical work in the world. Nelson Freire, Guiomar Novaes and Bidu Sayão were performers of global reputation, and OSESP is the reference orchestra. Where: Rio and São Paulo.

- [Colonial music](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/classica-colonial.html) (since 1760): Masses and motets from the churches of Minas, Bahia and Rio: Lobo de Mesquita and Father José Maurício Nunes Garcia.
- [Romanticism](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/classica-romantica.html) (since 1861): Opera and parlour music of the Empire: Carlos Gomes of 'O Guarani', and Alberto Nepomuceno.
- [Nationalism](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/classica-nacionalista.html) (since 1910): Villa-Lobos, Mignone, Camargo Guarnieri and Guerra-Peixe used popular rhythms and melodies in concert music.
- [Contemporary music](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/classica-contemporanea.html) (since 1963): From Gilberto Mendes's Música Nova manifesto (1963) to Marlos Nobre and Almeida Prado.
- [Performers, orchestras and choirs](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/classica-interpretes.html) (since 1911): Guiomar Novaes, Bidu Sayão, Nelson Freire, João Carlos Martins, Antonio Meneses and OSESP.

### [Folk Traditions](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/regional.html) (since 1800)

The music that lives in festivals, terreiros and circles: frevo and maracatu in Pernambuco, coco, ciranda and repente in the Northeast, jongo in the Southeast, catira, chamamé, siriri and cururu in the Centre-West, caiçara fandango on the coast of the South and São Paulo, gaúcho music, bumba-meu-boi, marchinhas and the rhythms of capoeira. Where: Every region.

- [Frevo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/frevo.html) (since 1907; UNESCO intangible heritage · 2012): The frantic rhythm of Recife and Olinda carnival, with colourful umbrellas; UNESCO heritage.
- [Maracatu](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/maracatu.html) (since 1800): Maracatu nações with alfaia drums and an Afro-Brazilian royal procession; the base of manguebeat.
- [Coco and ciranda](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/coco-embolada.html) (since 1900): Circle songs of the northeastern coast: Jackson do Pandeiro, Lia de Itamaracá, Selma do Coco.
- [Repente and cantoria](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/repente.html) (since 1800): Rhymed improvisation of duelling viola singers; Brazil's original rap battle.
- [Jongo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/jongo.html) (since 1800; Brazilian heritage · IPHAN 2005): A circle dance with Bantu-rooted drums and riddling songs, from the Paraíba Valley to Rio; one of samba's roots. Jongo da Serrinha.
- [Afro-Brazilian chants](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/cantos-afro.html) (since 1800): Vissungos and terreiro chants keep African languages alive; Clementina de Jesus and Os Tincoãs took them to record.
- [Catira / cateretê](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/catira.html) (since 1800): A caipira dance of handclaps and foot-stamping to the viola, alive in Goiás, Minas and rural São Paulo.
- [Chamamé](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/chamame.html) (since 1930): An accordion rhythm from the Argentina and Paraguay border, strong in Mato Grosso do Sul and Rio Grande do Sul.
- [Siriri and cururu](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/siriri-cururu.html) (since 1800): Dances and songs with viola de cocho and ganzá in the Cuiabá lowlands of Mato Grosso.
- [Caiçara fandango](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/fandango-caicara.html) (since 1800; Brazilian heritage · IPHAN 2012): Dances with viola, rabeca and wooden clogs in the caiçara communities of the Paraná and São Paulo coast.
- [Gaúcho / nativist music](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/musica-gaucha.html) (since 1950): Button accordion, vanerão and chamamé: Teixeirinha, Gaúcho da Fronteira, Renato Borghetti, Luiz Marenco.
- [Tchê music](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/tche-music.html) (since 1992): 1990s pop vanerão for dance halls: Tchê Garotos, Tchê Barbaridade.
- [Carnival marchinhas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/marchinhas.html) (since 1899): From 'Ó Abre Alas' (1899) to Lamartine Babo and Braguinha: Rio's street carnival.
- [Bumba-meu-boi and boi-bumbá](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/bumba-meu-boi.html) (since 1800; UNESCO intangible heritage · 2019): Maranhão and the Parintins Festival (Garantido vs Caprichoso) in Amazonas; UNESCO heritage.
- [Capoeira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/capoeira.html) (since 1800; UNESCO intangible heritage · 2014): Berimbau, atabaque and pandeiro lead the circle; Mestre Bimba and Mestre Pastinha.

### [Indigenous Music](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/indigena.html) (since 1500)

More than 300 Indigenous peoples live in Brazil, each with its own songs, flutes and maracas tied to ritual, work and memory. Pero Vaz de Caminha's letter (1500) already describes Indigenous people dancing; today artists such as Djuena Tikuna, Brô MC's and Kaê Guajajara carry these languages into rap, pop and song. Where: The whole territory, from the Amazon to the South.

- [Traditional songs](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/indigena-tradicional.html) (since 1500): Ritual, work and healing songs passed down orally; researchers such as Marlui Miranda recorded and spread this repertoire.
- [Contemporary Indigenous artists](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/subgenres/indigena-contemporanea.html) (since 2009): Rap, pop and song in native languages and in Portuguese: Brô MC's, Djuena Tikuna, Kaê Guajajara, Owerá.

### [Children's Music](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/infantil.html) (since 1982)

Xuxa sold the most popular children's records in the country's history in the 1980s; Turma do Balão Mágico and Trem da Alegria ruled TV. Today Galinha Pintadinha and Mundo Bita are among the most-watched children's channels on YouTube worldwide. Where: Television and YouTube.

- [Children's](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/genres/infantil.html) (since 1982): From 1980s TV to YouTube.

## Artists

### Samba (151)

- [Francisco Alves](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/francisco-alves.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1919 · tier S (Legend). Samba-canção, Samba-exaltação. The "King of Voice", the greatest singer of the radio era; first to record "Aquarela do Brasil" (1939).
- [Carmen Miranda](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/carmen-miranda.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1929 · tier S (Legend). Samba-canção, Carnival marchinhas. The "Brazilian Bombshell" took samba and marchinhas to Hollywood in the 1940s.
- [Cartola](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cartola.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1929 · tier S (Legend). Roots samba. Mangueira founder and author of "As Rosas Não Falam" and "O Mundo É um Moinho"; he recorded his first album at 65.
- [Noel Rosa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/noel-rosa.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1930 · tier S (Legend). Roots samba, Samba-canção. The "Poet of Vila Isabel": Rio chronicles in sambas such as "Com que Roupa?" and "Feitio de Oração".
- [Orlando Silva](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orlando-silva.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1934 · tier S (Legend). Samba-canção. The "Singer of the Crowds": "Carinhoso" (1937) and "Lábios Que Beijei".
- [Dorival Caymmi](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dorival-caymmi.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1938 · tier S (Legend). Samba-canção, Festival-era MPB. Singer of the sea and of Bahia: "O Que É Que a Baiana Tem?", "Marina", "Saudade da Bahia".
- [Elza Soares](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/elza-soares.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1959 · tier S (Legend). Samba-jazz, Brazilian soul, New MPB. From 1960s syncopated samba to the reinvention of "A Mulher do Fim do Mundo" (2015); named singer of the millennium by the BBC in 1999.
- [Jorge Ben Jor](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jorge-ben-jor.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1963 · tier S (Legend). Samba-rock, Brazilian soul, Samba-soul. Created samba-rock with a unique guitar and swing: "Mas Que Nada", "País Tropical", "Taj Mahal".
- [Paulinho da Viola](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/paulinho-da-viola.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1964 · tier S (Legend). Roots samba, Choro. Portela's elegance in "Foi um Rio que Passou em Minha Vida" and "Coração Leviano".
- [Beth Carvalho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/beth-carvalho.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1965 · tier S (Legend). Pagode, Roots samba. The "godmother of samba" revealed Cacique de Ramos pagode and Zeca Pagodinho: "Vou Festejar".
- [Clara Nunes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/clara-nunes.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · debut 1966 · tier S (Legend). Roots samba. The first Brazilian woman singer to sell over 100,000 copies: "Canto das Três Raças", "Conto de Areia".
- [Martinho da Vila](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/martinho-da-vila.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1967 · tier S (Legend). Roots samba, Samba-enredo, Partido-alto. Vila Isabel; "Canta Canta, Minha Gente", "Disritmia", "Mulheres".
- [Fundo de Quintal](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/fundo-de-quintal.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1980 · tier S (Legend). Pagode. Born at Cacique de Ramos, it created the language of pagode with banjo, tantã and hand repique.
- [Zeca Pagodinho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/zeca-pagodinho.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1983 · tier S (Legend). Pagode, Roots samba. Brazil's most popular sambista: "Deixa a Vida Me Levar", "Verdade", "Vai Vadiar".
- [Grupo Menos é Mais](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/grupo-menos-e-mais.html): Band · Federal District (Brasília) · tier S (Legend). Pagode. A Brasília group that took the samba circle to the top of streaming in the 2020s.
- [Donga](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/donga.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1917 · tier A (Giant). Roots samba. Registered "Pelo Telefone" (1917), regarded as the first recorded samba.
- [Mário Reis](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mario-reis.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1928 · tier A (Giant). Roots samba. Sang samba in a conversational tone, without the period's big-voiced style; recorded Sinhô and Noel Rosa and teamed up with Francisco Alves.
- [Ary Barroso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ary-barroso.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · debut 1930 · tier A (Giant). Samba-canção, Samba-exaltação. "Aquarela do Brasil" (1939), the exaltation samba that became the country's sonic postcard.
- [Sílvio Caldas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/silvio-caldas.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1930 · tier A (Giant). Samba-canção. "Chão de Estrelas" (1937) and a long radio-era career.
- [Dalva de Oliveira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dalva-de-oliveira.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1937 · tier A (Giant). Samba-canção. From Trio de Ouro to the "Queen of Voice": "Tudo Acabado", "Errei, Sim".
- [Nelson Cavaquinho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nelson-cavaquinho.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1940 · tier A (Giant). Roots samba. Sambas of rare melancholy and beauty: "A Flor e o Espinho", "Juízo Final".
- [Adoniran Barbosa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/adoniran-barbosa.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1941 · tier A (Giant). Roots samba. São Paulo samba with an Italian accent: "Trem das Onze", "Saudosa Maloca".
- [Nelson Gonçalves](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nelson-goncalves.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1941 · tier A (Giant). Samba-canção. "A Volta do Boêmio" (1956); one of the country's biggest record sellers.
- [Demônios da Garoa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/demonios-da-garoa.html): Group · São Paulo · debut 1943 · tier A (Giant). Roots samba. The interpreters of Adoniran Barbosa: "Trem das Onze", "Saudosa Maloca".
- [Elizeth Cardoso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/elizeth-cardoso.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1950 · tier A (Giant). Samba-canção, Bossa nova. "The Divine"; "Canção do Amor Demais" (1958) is an early bossa nova landmark.
- [Cauby Peixoto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cauby-peixoto.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1951 · tier A (Giant). Samba-canção. "Conceição" (1956) and a six-decade career.
- [Ângela Maria](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/angela-maria.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1951 · tier A (Giant). Samba-canção. "Sapoti", one of the most popular singers of the 1950s and 1960s.
- [Maysa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/maysa.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1956 · tier A (Giant). Samba-canção, Bossa nova. Heartbreak samba-canção: "Meu Mundo Caiu" and "Ouça".
- [Jair Rodrigues](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jair-rodrigues.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1962 · tier A (Giant). Roots samba, Festival-era MPB. "Disparada" (1966) and "Deixa Isso pra Lá"; Elis's partner on "Dois na Bossa".
- [Clementina de Jesus](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/clementina-de-jesus.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1964 · tier A (Giant). Roots samba, Partido-alto, Jongo, Afro-Brazilian chants. The voice of Black ancestry, revealed at 63; jongos, partido-alto and sambas de terreiro.
- [Dona Ivone Lara](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dona-ivone-lara.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1965 · tier A (Giant). Roots samba. The first woman to write a samba-enredo for a samba school; "Sonho Meu", "Alguém Me Avisou".
- [Bezerra da Silva](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bezerra-da-silva.html): Solo · Pernambuco · debut 1969 · tier A (Giant). Partido-alto, Roots samba. The "ambassador of the hills": partido-alto and crime chronicles, "Malandragem Dá um Tempo".
- [Alcione](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/alcione.html): Solo · Maranhão · debut 1972 · tier A (Giant). Roots samba, Samba-canção. The "Marrom": "Não Deixe o Samba Morrer", "Você Me Vira a Cabeça".
- [Leci Brandão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/leci-brandao.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1975 · tier A (Giant). Roots samba. The first woman in Mangueira's songwriters' wing; "Zé do Caroço".
- [Jorge Aragão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jorge-aragao.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1976 · tier A (Giant). Pagode. Fundo de Quintal founder and composer of "Coisinha do Pai" and "Vou Festejar".
- [Arlindo Cruz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/arlindo-cruz.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1981 · tier A (Giant). Pagode. Fundo de Quintal's banjo and author of hundreds of sambas: "Meu Lugar", "O Show Tem Que Continuar".
- [Raça Negra](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/raca-negra.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1983 · tier A (Giant). Romantic pagode. A pioneer of São Paulo romantic pagode: "Cheia de Manias", "É Tarde Demais".
- [Exaltasamba](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/exaltasamba.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1986 · tier A (Giant). Romantic pagode. Revealed Thiaguinho and Péricles: "Tá Vendo Aquela Lua", "Viver Sem Ti".
- [Péricles](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/pericles.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1986 · tier A (Giant). Romantic pagode. Exaltasamba's voice and a successful solo career.
- [Molejo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/molejo.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1988 · tier A (Giant). Pagode. Good-humoured pagode: "Cilindrada" and "Dança da Vassoura".
- [Só Pra Contrariar](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/so-pra-contrariar.html): Band · Minas Gerais · debut 1989 · tier A (Giant). Romantic pagode. With Alexandre Pires, the best-selling pagode of the 1990s: "Que Se Chama Amor", "Sai da Minha Aba".
- [Belo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/belo.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1993 · tier A (Giant). Romantic pagode. Soweto's voice and later one of the biggest solo careers in romantic pagode.
- [Turma do Pagode](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/turma-do-pagode.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1995 · tier A (Giant). Romantic pagode. São Paulo pagode: "Lancinho", "Deixa em Off".
- [Sorriso Maroto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sorriso-maroto.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1997 · tier A (Giant). Romantic pagode. Rio romantic pagode: "Sinais", "Ainda Gosto de Você".
- [Seu Jorge](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/seu-jorge.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1998 · tier A (Giant). Samba-rock, Brazilian soul, Samba-soul. From Farofa Carioca to film ("City of God", "The Life Aquatic"); "Burguesinha".
- [Alexandre Pires](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/alexandre-pires.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · debut 2001 · tier A (Giant). Romantic pagode, Pagonejo. Former Só Pra Contrariar singer, solo since 2001 with ballads and samba.
- [Thiaguinho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/thiaguinho.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 2002 · tier A (Giant). Romantic pagode. From Exaltasamba to the "Tardezinha" project, the biggest pagode name of the 2010s–20s.
- [Dilsinho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dilsinho.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 2014 · tier A (Giant). Romantic pagode. Romantic pagode: "Refém", "Péssimo Negócio".
- [Ferrugem](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ferrugem.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 2014 · tier A (Giant). Romantic pagode, Pagonejo. Pagode's new generation: "Pirata e Tesouro", "Climatizar".
- [Ataulfo Alves](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ataulfo-alves.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier A (Giant). Roots samba, Samba-canção. Author of "Ai, Que Saudades da Amélia", with Mário Lago.
- [Candeia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/candeia.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Roots samba, Partido-alto. Portela sambista and founder of the Quilombo school, a champion of roots samba.
- [Dick Farney](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dick-farney.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Samba-canção. Singer and pianist of "Copacabana" (1946), a forerunner of bossa nova.
- [Geraldo Pereira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/geraldo-pereira.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier A (Giant). Roots samba. Master of syncopated samba, of "Falsa Baiana".
- [Herivelto Martins](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/herivelto-martins.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Samba-canção. Songwriter of "Ave Maria no Morro" and creator of Trio de Ouro.
- [Ismael Silva](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ismael-silva.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Roots samba. Founder of Deixa Falar, the first samba school, and author of "Se Você Jurar".
- [Lupicínio Rodrigues](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/lupicinio-rodrigues.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · tier A (Giant). Samba-canção. The poet of heartbreak songs, of "Vingança" and "Nervos de Aço".
- [Monarco](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/monarco.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Roots samba. Composer and voice of the Velha Guarda da Portela.
- [Neguinho da Beija-Flor](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/neguinho-da-beija-flor.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Samba-enredo. Beija-Flor's official samba singer for almost fifty years.
- [Paulo Moura](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/paulo-moura.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Samba de gafieira, Brazilian jazz. Saxophonist and clarinettist who took gafieira to the concert stage.
- [Tamba Trio](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tamba-trio.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Samba-jazz. Luiz Eça's Rio samba-jazz trio.
- [Velha Guarda da Portela](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/velha-guarda-da-portela.html): Group · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Roots samba. Portela's veteran masters, guardians of terreiro samba.
- [Vicente Celestino](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/vicente-celestino.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Samba-canção. An operatic radio-era tenor: "O Ébrio" and "Coração Materno".
- [Wilson Batista](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/wilson-batista.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Roots samba. Composer of "Chico Brito" and of the famous song feud with Noel Rosa.
- [Zimbo Trio](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/zimbo-trio.html): Band · São Paulo · tier A (Giant). Samba-jazz. São Paulo samba-jazz trio.
- [Moreira da Silva](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/moreira-da-silva.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1934 · tier B (Reference). Roots samba, Samba de breque. Creator of samba de breque, with pauses for streetwise spoken lines.
- [Orquestra Tabajara](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-tabajara.html): Group · Paraíba · debut 1934 · tier B (Reference). Samba de gafieira. Severino Araújo's orchestra, the reference for gafieira dances; founded in 1934 in João Pessoa.
- [Riachão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/riachao.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1943 · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Samba/Pagode Album.
- [Dolores Duran](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dolores-duran.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1952 · tier B (Reference). Samba-canção. Songwriter and singer of "A Noite do Meu Bem" and "Por Causa de Você".
- [Zé Kéti](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ze-keti.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1955 · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. "A Voz do Morro" and "Máscara Negra".
- [Originais do Samba](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/originais-do-samba.html): Group · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1960 · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. The group where Mussum, of Os Trapalhões, started.
- [Benito di Paula](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/benito-di-paula.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1971 · tier B (Reference). Samba-canção. "Retalhos de Cetim" and "Charlie Brown".
- [João Nogueira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/joao-nogueira.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1972 · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. Founder of the Clube do Samba; Diogo Nogueira's father.
- [Agepê](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/agepe.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1975 · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. "Deixa Eu Te Amar"; the album "Mistura Brasileira" (1984) passed a million copies.
- [Almir Guineto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/almir-guineto.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1981 · tier B (Reference). Pagode, Partido-alto. Co-founder of Fundo de Quintal; "Mel na Boca".
- [Jovelina Pérola Negra](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jovelina-perola-negra.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1985 · tier B (Reference). Pagode. A voice of 1980s Rio pagode.
- [Katinguelê](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/katinguele.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1985 · tier B (Reference). Romantic pagode. São Paulo pagode with "Recado à Minha Amada".
- [Art Popular](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/art-popular.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1987 · tier B (Reference). Romantic pagode. "Temporal" and "Pimpolho".
- [Negritude Júnior](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/negritude-junior.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1987 · tier B (Reference). Romantic pagode. São Paulo pagode with "Cohab City".
- [Grupo Revelação](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/grupo-revelacao.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1991 · tier B (Reference). Pagode. With Xande de Pilares; "Deixa Acontecer", "Velocidade da Luz".
- [Soweto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/soweto.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1991 · tier B (Reference). Romantic pagode. The romantic pagode group that revealed Belo.
- [Pixote](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/pixote.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1993 · tier B (Reference). Romantic pagode. São Paulo pagode with "Insegurança".
- [Teresa Cristina](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/teresa-cristina.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1998 · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. Interpreter from Rio's Lapa and of the pandemic samba livestreams.
- [Monobloco](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/monobloco.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 2000 · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Samba/Pagode Album.
- [Inimigos da HP](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/inimigos-da-hp.html): Group · debut 2001 · tier B (Reference). Pagode. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Samba/Pagode Album.
- [Diogo Nogueira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/diogo-nogueira.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 2007 · tier B (Reference). Roots samba, Pagode. João Nogueira's son; roots samba for new generations.
- [Oba Oba Samba House](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/oba-oba-samba-house.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 2012 · tier B (Reference). Pagode, Pagonejo. A Ribeirão Preto group mixing samba and house; albums "Pagofunk" (2016) and "Pagonejo" (2018).
- [Anaí Rosa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/anai-rosa.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Samba/Pagode Album.
- [Anísio Silva](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/anisio-silva.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). Samba-canção. A romantic bolero singer and a top seller in the late 1950s.
- [Arlindinho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/arlindinho.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Pagode, Roots samba. Singer-songwriter, son of Arlindo Cruz.
- [Atitude 67](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/atitude-67.html): Band · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Pagode. Campinas group mixing pagode, pop and reggae.
- [Bebeto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bebeto.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Samba-rock. The "King of Samba-Rock" of São Paulo dance parties.
- [Beto sem Braço](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/beto-sem-braco.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Samba-enredo. A singer and songwriter, one of the great names of Império Serrano.
- [Billy Blanco](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/billy-blanco.html): Solo · Pará · tier B (Reference). Samba-canção, Bossa nova. A songwriter from Pará, of "Tereza da Praia" with Tom Jobim and the "Sinfonia do Rio de Janeiro".
- [Bokaloka](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bokaloka.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Romantic pagode. A pagode group from Rio, also spelled Boka Loka; it started as Água na Boca and took its name in 1999. The live album "Bokaloka de Verdade" (2001) went gold: "Mais Uma Chance", "Não Pedi pra Me Apaixonar".
- [Cláudio Jorge](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/claudio-jorge.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Samba/Pagode Album.
- [Cristina Buarque](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cristina-buarque.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. A singer and researcher who preserved the memory of Rio and São Paulo samba.
- [Dicró](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dicro.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. A singer of satirical sambas, in the line of Moreira da Silva and Bezerra da Silva.
- [Doce Encontro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/doce-encontro.html): Band · tier B (Reference). Romantic pagode. A 1990s romantic pagode group.
- [Dom Salvador](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dom-salvador.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Samba-jazz, Brazilian soul, Samba-funk. Pianist of samba-jazz and Brazilian soul.
- [Dona Edith do Prato](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dona-edith-do-prato.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). Samba de roda. Samba de roda singer from Santo Amaro who played plate and knife.
- [Doris Monteiro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/doris-monteiro.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Samba-canção, Bossa nova. A singer and actress of the shift from samba-canção to bossa nova.
- [Dudu Nobre](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dudu-nobre.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Pagode. A cavaquinho player, singer and samba songwriter, Zeca Pagodinho's godson.
- [Délcio Luiz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/delcio-luiz.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Pagode. Songwriter of "Cilada", "Marrom Bombom" and "40 Graus de Amor".
- [Ed Lincoln](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ed-lincoln.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Sambalanço. Organist and dance-band leader who made sambalanço dance.
- [Eliana de Lima](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/eliana-de-lima.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Pagode. A samba-school lead singer; "Desejo de Amar" (1991).
- [Ellen de Lima](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ellen-de-lima.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). Samba-canção. A radio-era voice, the singer of "Canção das Misses".
- [Elton Medeiros](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/elton-medeiros.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. Composer who partnered with Cartola and Paulinho da Viola.
- [Germano Mathias](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/germano-mathias.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Samba de breque. São Paulo's "professor of samba", a master of syncopated samba and samba de breque.
- [Grupo Bom Gosto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/grupo-bom-gosto.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Pagode. A Rio pagode group of the 2000s.
- [Grupo Raça](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/grupo-raca.html): Band · tier B (Reference). Pagode. A pagode group of the 1980s and 1990s.
- [Heitor dos Prazeres](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/heitor-dos-prazeres.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. Songwriter, singer and painter, a pioneer of samba and of the first samba schools.
- [Imaginasamba](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/imaginasamba.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Pagode. A Rio pagode group of the 2000s and 2010s.
- [Leandro Sapucahy](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/leandro-sapucahy.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. A samba producer, singer and percussionist.
- [Luiz Ayrão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/luiz-ayrao.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. "Os Amantes" (1977) sold about two million copies.
- [Luiz Carlos da Vila](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/luiz-carlos-da-vila.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba, Samba-enredo. A Vila Isabel songwriter, co-author of "Kizomba, Festa da Raça" (1988).
- [Luiz Eça](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/luiz-eca.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Samba-jazz. Pianist and leader of Tamba Trio.
- [Mariene de Castro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mariene-de-castro.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). Samba de roda, Roots samba. Bahian singer of samba de roda and the songs of the Recôncavo.
- [Marisa Gata Mansa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/marisa-gata-mansa.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Samba-canção. A singer and songwriter of 1950s and 1960s samba-canção.
- [Mart'nália](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mart-nalia.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. Martinho da Vila's daughter; samba and MPB.
- [Marvvila](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/marvvila.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Pagode. A Rio singer of the new pagode generation.
- [Mauro Diniz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mauro-diniz.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. Cavaquinho player and composer, son of Monarco.
- [Miltinho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/miltinho.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Sambalanço. A singer with a unique rhythmic phrasing, one of the voices of sambalanço.
- [Moacyr Luz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/moacyr-luz.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. A Rio songwriter who leads the Samba do Trabalhador.
- [Mumuzinho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mumuzinho.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Pagode. Pagode and TV; a coach on The Voice Kids.
- [Nei Lopes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nei-lopes.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba, Partido-alto. Composer, writer and researcher of Afro-Brazilian culture.
- [Nelson Sargento](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nelson-sargento.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. A Mangueira sambista, composer of "Agoniza Mas Não Morre".
- [Nilze Carvalho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nilze-carvalho.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Samba/Pagode Album.
- [Noite Ilustrada](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/noite-ilustrada.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. A singer and guitarist who recorded Paulo Vanzolini's "Volta por Cima".
- [Nora Ney](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nora-ney.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Samba-canção. Samba-canção singer of "Ninguém Me Ama" (1952).
- [Noriel Vilela](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/noriel-vilela.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Samba-rock. A deep-bass voice that joined samba-rock with Afro-Brazilian religious themes: "Só o Ôme".
- [Orlandivo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orlandivo.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Sambalanço. Singer-songwriter who defined 1960s sambalanço.
- [Os Travessos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/os-travessos.html): Band · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Romantic pagode. The pagode group that revealed Rodriguinho.
- [Otília Amorim](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/otilia-amorim.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. A revue-theatre actress and singer born in 1894, one of the first voices of samba on record.
- [Pedro Miranda](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/pedro-miranda.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Samba/Pagode Album.
- [Pique Novo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/pique-novo.html): Band · tier B (Reference). Romantic pagode. A 1990s romantic pagode group.
- [Pretinho da Serrinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/pretinho-da-serrinha.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. A samba singer, percussionist, arranger and producer.
- [Reinaldo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/reinaldo.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Romantic pagode, Pagode. The "Prince of Pagode", one of the forerunners of romantic pagode in the 1980s.
- [Roberto Ribeiro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/roberto-ribeiro.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba, Samba-enredo. An Império Serrano samba singer and songwriter.
- [Rodriguinho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/rodriguinho.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Romantic pagode. Former Os Travessos singer, now solo.
- [Silas de Oliveira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/silas-de-oliveira.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Samba-enredo. The great samba-enredo composer of Império Serrano.
- [Sombrinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sombrinha.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Pagode, Partido-alto. Singer, songwriter and cavaquinho player who was a member of Fundo de Quintal.
- [Swing & Simpatia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/swing-e-simpatia.html): Band · tier B (Reference). Pagode. A 2000s pagode group.
- [Thiago Garcia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/thiago-garcia.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Pagode. A pagode singer from Realengo, in Rio, who won The Voice Brasil 2025, the first season on SBT, on Mumuzinho's team.
- [Tiee](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tiee.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Romantic pagode. Romantic pagode singer.
- [Toninho Geraes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/toninho-geraes.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Pagode. A songwriter from Minas Gerais, of "Mulheres", a Martinho da Vila hit.
- [Victor Alves](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/victor-alves.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Romantic pagode. A singer from Macaé (Rio de Janeiro) who won The Voice Brasil 2020 on Iza's team.
- [Vou Zuar](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/vou-zuar.html): Band · tier B (Reference). Pagode. A 2010s pagode group.
- [Wander Pires](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/wander-pires.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Samba-enredo. A Rio samba-enredo singer.
- [Wilson das Neves](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/wilson-das-neves.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba. A legendary drummer who became a samba singer.
- [Wilson Moreira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/wilson-moreira.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Roots samba, Partido-alto. Partido-alto and jongo sambista, partner of Nei Lopes.
- [Xande de Pilares](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/xande-de-pilares.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Pagode. Formerly of Grupo Revelação; "Xande Canta Caetano" (2023).

### Choro (16)

- [Pixinguinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/pixinguinha.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1911 · tier S (Legend). Choro. Choro's greatest name: "Carinhoso", "Rosa", "Lamentos"; flautist, saxophonist and arranger.
- [Chiquinha Gonzaga](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/chiquinha-gonzaga.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1877 · tier A (Giant). Choro, Maxixe. The first choro pianist and the country's first woman conductor; "Ó Abre Alas" (1899), the first carnival march.
- [Ernesto Nazareth](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ernesto-nazareth.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1878 · tier A (Giant). Choro, Maxixe. Brazilian tangos and piano polkas that fed choro: "Odeon", "Brejeiro".
- [Jacob do Bandolim](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jacob-do-bandolim.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1940 · tier A (Giant). Choro. Mandolinist and composer of "Noites Cariocas" and "Doce de Coco"; founded Época de Ouro.
- [Zequinha de Abreu](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/zequinha-de-abreu.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier A (Giant). Choro. Author of "Tico-Tico no Fubá" (1917).
- [Época de Ouro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/epoca-de-ouro.html): Group · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Choro. Choro ensemble founded by Jacob do Bandolim.
- [Waldir Azevedo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/waldir-azevedo.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1949 · tier B (Reference). Choro. Cavaquinho virtuoso; "Brasileirinho" (1949) became the world's best-known choro.
- [Altamiro Carrilho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/altamiro-carrilho.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1950 · tier B (Reference). Choro. A flautist of technique and humour, heir to Pixinguinha.
- [Hamilton de Holanda](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/hamilton-de-holanda.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1990 · tier B (Reference). Choro, Brazilian jazz. Ten-string mandolin between choro and jazz; a Latin Grammy winner.
- [Yamandu Costa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/yamandu-costa.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1998 · tier B (Reference). Choro, Gaúcho / nativist music, Brazilian guitar. Seven-string guitar of rare virtuosity, from chamamé to choro.
- [Catulo da Paixão Cearense](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/catulo-da-paixao-cearense.html): Solo · Maranhão · tier B (Reference). Modinha and lundu. Poet and singer of the modinha, lyricist of "Luar do Sertão".
- [Joaquim Callado](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/joaquim-callado.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Choro. Flautist regarded as the father of choro, in the 1870s.
- [Nailor Proveta](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nailor-proveta.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Choro, Brazilian jazz. Clarinettist and saxophonist of Banda Mantiqueira.
- [Nó em Pingo d'Água](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/no-em-pingo-d-agua.html): Group · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Choro. Rio choro and instrumental group.
- [Rabo de Lagartixa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/rabo-de-lagartixa.html): Group · tier B (Reference). Choro. A choro group.
- [Xisto Bahia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/xisto-bahia.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). Modinha and lundu. 19th-century Bahian actor and composer of lundus such as "Isto É Bom".

### Bossa Nova (26)

- [Tom Jobim](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tom-jobim.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1956 · tier S (Legend). Bossa nova, Festival-era MPB. The most recorded Brazilian composer in the world: "The Girl from Ipanema", "Águas de Março", "Wave".
- [Vinicius de Moraes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/vinicius-de-moraes.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1956 · tier S (Legend). Bossa nova, Festival-era MPB, Afro-samba. The "poetinha": bossa nova's lyricist and partner of Jobim, Baden and Toquinho.
- [João Gilberto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/joao-gilberto.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1958 · tier S (Legend). Bossa nova. The guitar beat and minimal voice of "Chega de Saudade" invented bossa nova.
- [Baden Powell](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/baden-powell.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1955 · tier A (Giant). Bossa nova, Brazilian guitar, Afro-samba. Afro-samba guitar with Vinicius: "Berimbau", "Canto de Ossanha".
- [Carlos Lyra](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/carlos-lyra.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1958 · tier A (Giant). Bossa nova. "Minha Namorada", "Você e Eu", "Coisa Mais Linda".
- [Roberto Menescal](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/roberto-menescal.html): Solo · Espírito Santo · debut 1958 · tier A (Giant). Bossa nova. "O Barquinho", "Rio" and the guitar of the first generation.
- [Sérgio Mendes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sergio-mendes.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1961 · tier A (Giant). Bossa nova, Brazilian jazz. Brasil '66 and "Mas Que Nada" made him the most popular Brazilian in the US; a Grammy in 1992.
- [Astrud Gilberto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/astrud-gilberto.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1963 · tier A (Giant). Bossa nova. The voice of "The Girl from Ipanema" on Getz/Gilberto; an international career.
- [Marcos Valle](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/marcos-valle.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1963 · tier A (Giant). Bossa nova, Brazilian soul. "Samba de Verão" and, later, the 1970s groove rediscovered by DJs.
- [Nara Leão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nara-leao.html): Solo · Espírito Santo · debut 1963 · tier A (Giant). Bossa nova, Festival-era MPB, Tropicália. The "muse of bossa nova" who became a protest voice and then a tropicalist.
- [Toquinho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/toquinho.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1964 · tier A (Giant). Bossa nova, Festival-era MPB. Vinicius's partner: "Aquarela", "Tarde em Itapuã", "O Caderno".
- [Os Cariocas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/os-cariocas.html): Group · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1942 · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova. Bossa nova's vocal group.
- [Johnny Alf](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/johnny-alf.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1952 · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova. Pianist who prefigured bossa nova: "Rapaz de Bem", "Eu e a Brisa".
- [Leny Andrade](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/leny-andrade.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1958 · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova, Samba-jazz. The "first lady of Brazilian jazz".
- [Joyce Moreno](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/joyce-moreno.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1968 · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova. Guitarist and songwriter with a career in Japan and Europe.
- [Bebel Gilberto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bebel-gilberto.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1986 · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova, New MPB. "Tanto Tempo" (2000) renewed bossa nova for a global audience.
- [Bossacucanova](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bossacucanova.html): Band · debut 1999 · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Contemporary Pop Album.
