- [Alaíde Costa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/alaide-costa.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova, Festival-era MPB. A delicate bossa nova voice with a career of more than six decades.
- [Celso Fonseca](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/celso-fonseca.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Song and the Latin Grammy for Best MPB Album.
- [Claudette Soares](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/claudette-soares.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova. A Rio singer of bossa nova and MPB.
- [Maria Creuza](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/maria-creuza.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova. A singer from Bahia who toured with Vinicius de Moraes and Toquinho.
- [Miúcha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/miucha.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova. Chico Buarque's sister and Bebel Gilberto's mother; recorded with Tom Jobim and Stan Getz.
- [Paula Morelenbaum](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/paula-morelenbaum.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova. Sang alongside Tom Jobim for more than ten years before going solo.
- [Pery Ribeiro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/pery-ribeiro.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova. Son of Dalva de Oliveira and Herivelto Martins; one of the first to record "Garota de Ipanema".
- [Sylvia Telles](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sylvia-telles.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova. One of bossa nova's great interpreters; she died in 1966, aged 32.
- [Wanda Sá](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/wanda-sa.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Bossa nova. A bossa nova guitarist and singer.

### MPB (160)

- [Elis Regina](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/elis-regina.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1961 · tier S (Legend). Festival-era MPB. The "Pimentinha": MPB's greatest interpreter; "Arrastão", "Águas de Março", "Como Nossos Pais".
- [Gilberto Gil](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/gilberto-gil.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1962 · tier S (Legend). Tropicália, Festival-era MPB, Afoxé and ijexá. Tropicalist and former Minister of Culture: "Aquele Abraço", "Andar com Fé", "Palco".
- [Chico Buarque](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/chico-buarque.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1964 · tier S (Legend). Festival-era MPB. Songwriter and novelist; "A Banda", "Construção", "Apesar de Você" dodged the censors.
- [Caetano Veloso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/caetano-veloso.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1965 · tier S (Legend). Tropicália, Festival-era MPB. Tropicália's leader and one of Latin America's most influential artists: "Alegria, Alegria", "Sozinho".
- [Gal Costa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/gal-costa.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1965 · tier S (Legend). Tropicália, Festival-era MPB. Tropicália's voice: "Baby", "Divino, Maravilhoso", "Chuva de Prata".
- [Maria Bethânia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/maria-bethania.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1965 · tier S (Legend). Festival-era MPB. Dramatic interpreter and Caetano's sister: "Carcará", "Explode Coração".
- [Milton Nascimento](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/milton-nascimento.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · debut 1967 · tier S (Legend). Clube da Esquina, Festival-era MPB. "Bituca": "Travessia", "Maria, Maria", "Canção da América"; admired by Wayne Shorter and Herbie Hancock.
- [Ney Matogrosso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ney-matogrosso.html): Solo · Mato Grosso do Sul · debut 1971 · tier S (Legend). Festival-era MPB, Psychedelic rock. From Secos & Molhados to the most theatrical solo career in Brazilian music.
- [Djavan](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/djavan.html): Solo · Alagoas · debut 1975 · tier S (Legend). Festival-era MPB, Brazilian soul. Sophisticated harmony and swing: "Flor de Lis", "Oceano", "Sina".
- [Marisa Monte](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/marisa-monte.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1988 · tier S (Legend). New MPB, Roots samba. The great MPB voice of the 1990s–2000s; Tribalistas; "Ainda Bem", "Amor I Love You".
- [Edu Lobo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/edu-lobo.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1962 · tier A (Giant). Festival-era MPB. Festival-era composer: "Arrastão", "Upa Neguinho", "Ponteio".
- [Tom Zé](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tom-ze.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1968 · tier A (Giant). Tropicália. The experimental tropicalist rediscovered by David Byrne in the 1990s.
- [Ivan Lins](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ivan-lins.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1970 · tier A (Giant). Festival-era MPB. A composer recorded by Quincy Jones and Ella Fitzgerald: "Madalena", "Começar de Novo".
- [Belchior](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/belchior.html): Solo · Ceará · debut 1971 · tier A (Giant). Festival-era MPB, Pessoal do Ceará. "Como Nossos Pais", "Apenas um Rapaz Latino-Americano"; vanished from public life in the 2000s.
- [Beto Guedes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/beto-guedes.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · debut 1971 · tier A (Giant). Clube da Esquina. "Amor de Índio", "Sol de Primavera", "O Sal da Terra".
- [Fagner](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/fagner.html): Solo · Ceará · debut 1971 · tier A (Giant). Festival-era MPB, Pessoal do Ceará. "Canteiros", "Borbulhas de Amor".
- [Alceu Valença](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/alceu-valenca.html): Solo · Pernambuco · debut 1972 · tier A (Giant). Festival-era MPB, Frevo. Frevo, maracatu and rock: "Anunciação", "Tropicana", "La Belle de Jour".
- [Clube da Esquina](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/clube-da-esquina.html): Collective · Minas Gerais · debut 1972 · tier A (Giant). Clube da Esquina. The Minas movement joining rock, bossa, jazz and folklore; the 1972 album is the landmark.
- [João Bosco](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/joao-bosco.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · debut 1972 · tier A (Giant). Festival-era MPB, Samba-jazz. With Aldir Blanc: "O Bêbado e a Equilibrista", "Kid Cavaquinho".
- [Lô Borges](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/lo-borges.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · debut 1972 · tier A (Giant). Clube da Esquina. "O Trem Azul", "Paisagem da Janela", "Um Girassol da Cor do Seu Cabelo".
- [Gonzaguinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/gonzaguinha.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1973 · tier A (Giant). Festival-era MPB. Luiz Gonzaga's son: "O Que É, O Que É?", "Explode Coração".
- [Moraes Moreira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/moraes-moreira.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1975 · tier A (Giant). Festival-era MPB, Axé music. From Novos Baianos to the trio elétrico, where he was the first to sing; "Pombo Correio".
- [Guilherme Arantes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/guilherme-arantes.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1976 · tier A (Giant). Festival-era MPB, Pop rock. "Meu Mundo e Nada Mais", "Planeta Água" and "Amanhã".
- [Zé Ramalho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ze-ramalho.html): Solo · Paraíba · debut 1977 · tier A (Giant). Festival-era MPB, Pé-de-serra forró. "Chão de Giz", "Admirável Gado Novo", "Frevo Mulher".
- [14 Bis](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/14-bis.html): Band · Minas Gerais · debut 1979 · tier A (Giant). Clube da Esquina, Pop rock. "Planeta Sonho", "Linda Juventude", "Todo Azul do Mar".
- [Lenine](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/lenine.html): Solo · Pernambuco · debut 1979 · tier A (Giant). Festival-era MPB, Pop rock. Percussive guitar from Pernambuco: "Na Pressão", "Paciência".
- [Arnaldo Antunes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/arnaldo-antunes.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1982 · tier A (Giant). New MPB, Pop rock. From Titãs to Tribalistas and visual poetry; "Saiba", "Socorro".
- [Adriana Calcanhotto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/adriana-calcanhotto.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1990 · tier A (Giant). New MPB. "Devolva-me", "Vambora", "Esquadros".
- [Ana Carolina](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ana-carolina.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · debut 1999 · tier A (Giant). New MPB. "Garganta", "Quem de Nós Dois" and "Encostar na Tua".
- [Tribalistas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tribalistas.html): Group · debut 2002 · tier A (Giant). New MPB. Marisa Monte, Arnaldo Antunes and Carlinhos Brown's trio; its 2002 album sold millions.
- [Silva](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/silva.html): Solo · Espírito Santo · debut 2012 · tier A (Giant). New MPB, Pop rock. Electronic pop and MPB: "Não Vá Embora", "Sorte" with Liniker.
- [Emílio Santiago](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/emilio-santiago.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Festival-era MPB, Samba-canção. The voice of the best-selling "Aquarela Brasileira" series.
- [Geraldo Vandré](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/geraldo-vandre.html): Solo · Paraíba · tier A (Giant). Festival-era MPB. Author of "Pra Não Dizer Que Não Falei das Flores" (1968), an anthem against the dictatorship.
- [Itamar Assumpção](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/itamar-assumpcao.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier A (Giant). Vanguarda Paulista. Singer-songwriter from Tietê, the central name of the Vanguarda Paulista.
- [Jards Macalé](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jards-macale.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Tropicália, Festival-era MPB. MPB's cult singer, guitarist and songwriter: "Vapor Barato" and "Gotham City".
- [Nana Caymmi](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nana-caymmi.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1960 · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Deep-voiced interpreter and Dorival Caymmi's daughter.
- [MPB4](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mpb4.html): Group · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1965 · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A vocal group from Niterói with a long partnership with Chico Buarque.
- [Antônio Carlos e Jocáfi](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/antonio-carlos-e-jocafi.html): Duo · Bahia · debut 1969 · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A duo from Bahia, of "Você Abusou" and many soap-opera themes.
- [Luiz Cláudio Ramos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/luiz-claudio-ramos.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1969 · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Arrangement.
- [Banda de Pau e Corda](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/banda-de-pau-e-corda.html): Band · debut 1972 · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Roots Album.
- [Geraldo Azevedo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/geraldo-azevedo.html): Solo · Pernambuco · debut 1972 · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. "Dia Branco", "Táxi Lunar".
- [Ednardo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ednardo.html): Solo · Ceará · debut 1973 · tier B (Reference). Pessoal do Ceará. "Pavão Mysteriozo".
- [Luiz Melodia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/luiz-melodia.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1973 · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB, Brazilian soul. "Pérola Negra", "Magrelinha".
- [Simone](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/simone.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1973 · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. "Então É Natal", "Começar de Novo".
- [Fafá de Belém](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/fafa-de-belem.html): Solo · Pará · debut 1975 · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB, Carimbó. Pará's voice in MPB: "Filho da Bahia", "Vermelho".
- [Boca Livre](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/boca-livre.html): Group · debut 1978 · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Nominated for a Grammy.
- [Zizi Possi](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/zizi-possi.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1978 · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. "Perigo" and "Per Amore".
- [Joanna](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/joanna.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1979 · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A romantic interpreter with big hits in the 1980s and 1990s.
- [Ângela Ro Ro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/angela-ro-ro.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1979 · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. "Amor, Meu Grande Amor".
- [Zélia Duncan](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/zelia-duncan.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1990 · tier B (Reference). New MPB, Pop rock. "Catedral", "Pagu" with Rita Lee.
- [Thalma de Freitas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/thalma-de-freitas.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1992 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Nominated for a Grammy.
- [Paulinho Moska](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/paulinho-moska.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1993 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. "Pensando em Você" and "A Seta e o Alvo".
- [Chico César](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/chico-cesar.html): Solo · Paraíba · debut 1995 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. "Mama África", "À Primeira Vista".
- [Patrícia Bastos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/patricia-bastos.html): Solo · Amapá · debut 1997 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Roots Album.
- [Zeca Baleiro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/zeca-baleiro.html): Solo · Maranhão · debut 1997 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. "Salão de Beleza" and "Telegrama".
- [Vanessa da Mata](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/vanessa-da-mata.html): Solo · Mato Grosso · debut 2002 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. "Ai, Ai, Ai", "Boa Sorte/Good Luck" with Ben Harper.
- [Maria Rita](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/maria-rita.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 2003 · tier B (Reference). New MPB, Roots samba. Elis Regina's daughter; "A Festa", "Cara Valente".
- [Céu](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ceu.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 2005 · tier B (Reference). New MPB, Brazilian soul. Electronic MPB with international recognition.
- [Roberta Sá](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/roberta-sa.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Norte · debut 2005 · tier B (Reference). New MPB, Roots samba. Samba and MPB, from Natal to Rio.
- [Mallu Magalhães](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mallu-magalhaes.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 2007 · tier B (Reference). New MPB, Indie rock. Revealed on MySpace at 15; "Você Não Presta", "Velha e Louca".
- [Tiago Iorc](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tiago-iorc.html): Solo · Federal District (Brasília) · debut 2008 · tier B (Reference). New MPB, Alternative pop. "Amei Te Ver", "Coisa Linda".
- [5 a Seco](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/5-a-seco.html): Band · debut 2009 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best MPB Album.
- [Ellen Oléria](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ellen-oleria.html): Solo · Federal District (Brasília) · debut 2009 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Won the first season of The Voice Brasil (2012) on Carlinhos Brown's team; she mixes jazz, samba, pop and hip-hop. Album "Re.trato" (2022).
- [Maria Gadú](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/maria-gadu.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 2009 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. "Shimbalaiê" (2009).
- [Tim Bernardes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tim-bernardes.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 2009 · tier B (Reference). New MPB, Indie rock. O Terno's voice; "Recomeçar" (2017) and a collaboration with Fleet Foxes.
- [Marcelo Jeneci](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/marcelo-jeneci.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 2010 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. "Felicidade".
- [Tulipa Ruiz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tulipa-ruiz.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 2010 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. "Efêmera", "Pedrinho".
- [As Bahias e a Cozinha Mineira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/as-bahias-e-a-cozinha-mineira.html): Band · debut 2011 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Contemporary Pop Album.
- [Ayrton Montarroyos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ayrton-montarroyos.html): Solo · Pernambuco · debut 2011 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. A singer from Recife and a finalist on The Voice Brasil 2015; before the show he already had a Latin Grammy nomination for the album "Herivelto Martins - 100 Anos".
- [Rubel](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/rubel.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 2013 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. "Pearl" (2013) and "Casas" (2018).
- [Jadsa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jadsa.html): Solo · debut 2015 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Rock or Alternative Album.
- [Ana Frango Elétrico](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ana-frango-eletrico.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 2018 · tier B (Reference). New MPB, Indie rock. "Little Electric Chicken Heart" (2019).
- [Agnes Nunes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/agnes-nunes.html): Solo · Paraíba · debut 2019 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Discovered online; a deep voice and guitar.
- [Bala Desejo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bala-desejo.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 2021 · tier B (Reference). New MPB. The album "Sim Sim Sim" (2022), a Latin Grammy winner.

- [Alice Caymmi](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/alice-caymmi.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Dorival Caymmi's granddaughter, from MPB to pop.
- [Amelinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/amelinha.html): Solo · Ceará · tier B (Reference). Pessoal do Ceará. A singer from Ceará, of "Frevo Mulher" (1979).
- [Ana Cañas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ana-canas.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). New MPB. A São Paulo singer-songwriter of new MPB.
- [Anelis Assumpção](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/anelis-assumpcao.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Dub, reggae, afrobeat and samba; Itamar Assumpção's daughter.
- [Antonio Nóbrega](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/antonio-nobrega.html): Solo · Pernambuco · tier B (Reference). Armorial music, Frevo. Musician and dancer of Quinteto Armorial and Pernambuco folk culture.
- [Arrigo Barnabé](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/arrigo-barnabe.html): Solo · Paraná · tier B (Reference). Vanguarda Paulista. Author of "Clara Crocodilo" (1980), a landmark of the Vanguarda Paulista.
- [Assucena](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/assucena.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). New MPB, LGBTQIA+ pop. A trans singer and actress from Vitória da Conquista, formerly of As Baías and nominated for the Latin Grammy in 2019 and 2020; solo album "Lusco-Fusco" (2023).
- [Bia Ferreira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bia-ferreira.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). New MPB. "Black Women's Music": "Cota Não É Esmola".

- [Chico Chico](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/chico-chico.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Singer-songwriter, son of Cássia Eller.
- [Clarice Falcão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/clarice-falcao.html): Solo · Pernambuco · tier B (Reference). New MPB, Indie rock. A singer, actress and comedian; nominated for Best New Artist at the 2013 Latin Grammys.
- [Claudia Telles](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/claudia-telles.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A romantic interpreter of "Fim de Tarde" and "Eu Preciso Te Esquecer".
- [Cátia de França](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/catia-de-franca.html): Solo · Paraíba · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A singer-songwriter from Paraíba whose songs draw on literature.

- [Dora Morelenbaum](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dora-morelenbaum.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). New MPB. From Bala Desejo, a 2022 Latin Grammy winner, to a solo career.
- [Dori Caymmi](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dori-caymmi.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Arranger, guitarist and singer, Dorival Caymmi's son.

- [Elomar](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/elomar.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A composer and guitarist from the Bahia backlands, recorded by Fagner, Elba Ramalho and Xangai.

- [Gilsons](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/gilsons.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Gilberto Gil's sons and grandson: "Várias Queixas".
- [Giuliano Eriston](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/giuliano-eriston.html): Solo · Ceará · tier B (Reference). New MPB. A singer from Bela Cruz (Ceará) who won The Voice Brasil 2021 on Michel Teló's team.
- [Grupo Rumo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/grupo-rumo.html): Band · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Vanguarda Paulista. Luiz Tatit and Ná Ozzetti's group, which explored speech in song.
- [Hermes Aquino](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/hermes-aquino.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A singer from Rio Grande do Sul, of "Nuvem Passageira".

- [Jane Duboc](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jane-duboc.html): Solo · Pará · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Singer from Pará, the voice of Bacamarte's "Depois do Fim" (1983) and of a solo MPB career.
- [Jaques Morelenbaum](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jaques-morelenbaum.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Cellist, arranger and conductor; nominated for the Latin Grammy for Album of the Year as co-producer of Caetano Veloso's "Livro".
- [Jessé](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jesse.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. The powerful voice of "Porto Solidão" and "Voa Liberdade".
- [Jorge Mautner](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jorge-mautner.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Tropicália. A singer, violinist and writer, author of "Maracatu Atômico".
- [Jorge Vercillo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jorge-vercillo.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). New MPB. "Que Nem Maré" and "Monalisa".

- [Joyce Alane](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/joyce-alane.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Singer nominated for Best New Artist at the 2025 Prêmio Multishow.
- [Juca Chaves](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/juca-chaves.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A songwriter and comedian, the "minstrel" of satirical modinhas.
- [Julia Mestre](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/julia-mestre.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). New MPB. A singer, songwriter and bassist of Bala Desejo and of a solo career.
- [Kleiton & Kledir](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/kleiton-e-kledir.html): Duo · Rio Grande do Sul · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB, Gaúcho / nativist music. Brothers from Pelotas: "Deu pra Ti".
- [Larissa Luz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/larissa-luz.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Ex-Araketu, a voice of Bahian Afrofuturism.
- [Luciana Mello](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/luciana-mello.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). New MPB. A singer-songwriter, Jair Rodrigues's daughter.
- [Luiza Possi](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/luiza-possi.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). New MPB. An MPB and pop singer since the 2000s, Zizi Possi's daughter.
- [Maria Alcina](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/maria-alcina.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Won the 1972 International Song Festival with Jorge Ben's "Fio Maravilha".
- [Mariana Aydar](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mariana-aydar.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). New MPB, Pé-de-serra forró. A São Paulo singer of forró and MPB, a Latin Grammy winner.
- [Moreno Veloso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/moreno-veloso.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Singer and producer; nominated for the Latin Grammy for Producer of the Year for albums by Gilberto Gil and Caetano Veloso.
- [Mônica Salmaso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/monica-salmaso.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). New MPB. A singer with a broad repertoire and refined arrangements who revives seldom-heard songs.
- [Nilson Chaves](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nilson-chaves.html): Solo · Pará · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Roots Album.
- [Ná Ozzetti](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/na-ozzetti.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Vanguarda Paulista. The voice of Grupo Rumo and of a solo career in the São Paulo avant-garde.
- [Olivia Byington](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/olivia-byington.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A Rio singer, songwriter and guitarist.
- [Olívia Hime](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/olivia-hime.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Song.
- [Orlando Morais](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orlando-morais.html): Solo · Goiás · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist from Goiás.
- [Oswaldo Montenegro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/oswaldo-montenegro.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. "Bandolins" and "Lua e Flor".
- [Paulinho Pedra Azul](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/paulinho-pedra-azul.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A singer and poet from Minas Gerais, of "Jardim da Fantasia".
- [Paulo Diniz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/paulo-diniz.html): Solo · Pernambuco · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A singer-songwriter from Pernambuco, of "Quero Voltar pra Bahia".
- [Pedro Mariano](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/pedro-mariano.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). New MPB. A singer-songwriter, son of Elis Regina and César Camargo Mariano.
- [Peninha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/peninha.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Singer-songwriter of "Sonhos" and "Sozinho".
- [Premeditando o Breque](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/premeditando-o-breque.html): Band · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Vanguarda Paulista, Comic rock. Premê: São Paulo humour and samba from the Vanguarda Paulista.
- [Quinteto Armorial](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/quinteto-armorial.html): Group · Pernambuco · tier B (Reference). Armorial music. Movimento Armorial group that joined rabeca, viola and flute to concert music.
- [Quinteto Violado](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/quinteto-violado.html): Group · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Roots Album.
- [Rita Benneditto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/rita-benneditto.html): Solo · Maranhão · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Maranhão singer mixing MPB and Afro-Brazilian rhythms.
- [Roberta Campos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/roberta-campos.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). New MPB. More than twenty soap-opera songs, such as "De Janeiro a Janeiro".
- [Ruy Maurity](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ruy-maurity.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A singer-songwriter from Rio de Janeiro state, of 1970s and 1980s MPB.
- [Selma Reis](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/selma-reis.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A singer and actress from Rio de Janeiro state.
- [Sá & Guarabyra](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sa-e-guarabyra.html): Duo · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB, Rock rural. The "rural rock" of "Sobradinho".
- [Sérgio Ricardo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sergio-ricardo.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB, Bossa nova. A musician and filmmaker of bossa nova, Cinema Novo and protest song.
- [Sérgio Sampaio](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sergio-sampaio.html): Solo · Espírito Santo · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Author of "Eu Quero É Botar Meu Bloco na Rua" (1972), a cult name in MPB.
- [Sérgio Santos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sergio-santos.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Song.
- [Taiguara](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/taiguara.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A singer-songwriter born in Uruguay, one of the artists most censored by the dictatorship.
- [Tavito](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tavito.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Clube da Esquina. Songwriter of "Casa no Campo" (with Zé Rodrix) and "Rua Ramalhete".
- [Teca Calazans](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/teca-calazans.html): Solo · Espírito Santo · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Roots Album.
- [Tetê Espíndola](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tete-espindola.html): Solo · Mato Grosso do Sul · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A high, experimental voice from Mato Grosso do Sul; won the Festival dos Festivais with "Escrito nas Estrelas" (1985).
- [Tiê](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tie.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). New MPB. "Piscar o Olho" (2011) and "A Noite" (2014), soap-opera themes.
- [Tunai](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tunai.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Minas Gerais singer-songwriter.
- [Vander Lee](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/vander-lee.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Minas Gerais singer-songwriter.
- [Vinícius Cantuária](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/vinicius-cantuaria.html): Solo · Amazonas · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB, Bossa nova. A singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist from Amazonas, of "Só Você".
- [Virgínia Rodrigues](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/virginia-rodrigues.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Song.
- [Vital Farias](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/vital-farias.html): Solo · Paraíba · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A singer-songwriter from Paraíba, of "Saga da Amazônia".
- [Walter Franco](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/walter-franco.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB, Psychedelic rock. Experimental songwriter of "Cabeça" and "Vela Aberta".
- [Xangai](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/xangai.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A singer and viola player from southern Bahia.
- [Zeca Veloso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/zeca-veloso.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). New MPB. Nominated for Best New Artist at the 2026 Latin Grammys.
- [Zezé Motta](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/zeze-motta.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. An actress and singer, a leading figure of Afro-Brazilian culture.
- [Zé Ibarra](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ze-ibarra.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). New MPB. The high voice of Bala Desejo, a 2022 Latin Grammy winner, and of a solo career.
- [Zé Renato](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ze-renato.html): Solo · Espírito Santo · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. A singer and guitarist from Espírito Santo.
- [Áurea Martins](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/aurea-martins.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Festival-era MPB. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Roots Album.

### Brazilian Rock (509)

- [Roberto Carlos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/roberto-carlos.html): Solo · Espírito Santo · debut 1960 · tier S (Legend). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê, Pop rock. The "King": from Jovem Guarda's iê-iê-iê to romantic ballads.
- [Rita Lee](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/rita-lee.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1963 · tier S (Legend). Psychedelic rock, Pop rock. From Os Mutantes to a solo career: the "queen of Brazilian rock".
- [Os Mutantes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/os-mutantes.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1966 · tier S (Legend). Psychedelic rock, Tropicália. The backbone of Tropicália in rock: Anglo-American psychedelia and studio experimentation applied to Brazilian music.
- [Raul Seixas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/raul-seixas.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1967 · tier S (Legend). Psychedelic rock, Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê. The "maluco beleza": "Metamorfose Ambulante", "Gita", "Maluco Beleza".
- [Novos Baianos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/novos-baianos.html): Band · Bahia · debut 1969 · tier S (Legend). Psychedelic rock, Samba-rock. Fused samba, choro and rock with poetry and communal living; "Acabou Chorare" is one of Brazil's greatest records.
- [Secos & Molhados](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/secos-e-molhados.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1971 · tier S (Legend). Psychedelic rock. Glam theatricality and poetry; the 1973 debut broke sales records and revealed Ney Matogrosso.
- [Cazuza](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cazuza.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1980 · tier S (Legend). BRock (1980s), Pop rock. From Barão Vermelho to a solo career: "Exagerado", "Ideologia", "O Tempo Não Para".
- [Barão Vermelho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/barao-vermelho.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1981 · tier S (Legend). BRock (1980s), Hard rock. The Cazuza/Frejat partnership created urban blues-rock classics and defined 1980s radio rock.
- [Legião Urbana](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/legiao-urbana.html): Band · Federal District (Brasília) · debut 1982 · tier S (Legend). BRock (1980s), Post-punk / new wave, Brasília rock. Poetic, critical lyrics that became generational references; a cohesive catalogue even after the end in 1996.
- [Os Paralamas do Sucesso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/os-paralamas-do-sucesso.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1982 · tier S (Legend). BRock (1980s), Ska / reggae rock, Pop rock. Popularized the fusion of rock with reggae and ska, with a radio-friendly catalogue and social awareness.
- [Titãs](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/titas.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1982 · tier S (Legend). BRock (1980s), Punk, Pop rock. Constant versatility and reinvention; "Cabeça Dinossauro" is the turning point between punk, social critique and pop.
- [Sepultura](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sepultura.html): Band · Minas Gerais · debut 1984 · tier S (Legend). Thrash, death and black metal. Brazil's biggest metal export; "Chaos A.D." and "Roots" brought percussion and Indigenous themes into thrash.
- [Engenheiros do Hawaii](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/engenheiros-do-hawaii.html): Band · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1985 · tier S (Legend). BRock (1980s), Gaúcho rock. Rock of ideas with Humberto Gessinger's lyrics, clever arrangements and millions of records sold.
- [Chico Science & Nação Zumbi](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/chico-science-e-nacao-zumbi.html): Band · Pernambuco · debut 1991 · tier S (Legend). Manguebeat. Founders of manguebeat: maracatu, guitars and hip-hop with social critique; they put the Northeast back at the vanguard.
- [Charlie Brown Jr.](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/charlie-brown-jr.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1992 · tier S (Legend). Rap rock / nu metal, Hardcore, Alternative rock. Hardcore, rap, reggae and skate culture with massive choruses that ruled radio and TV from the late 90s through the 2000s.
- [Celly Campello](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/celly-campello.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1958 · tier A (Giant). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê. "Estúpido Cupido" (1959): Brazilian rock's first teen idol.
- [Erasmo Carlos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/erasmo-carlos.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1958 · tier A (Giant). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê, Pop rock. The "Tremendão", Roberto Carlos's partner and a Brazilian rock pioneer.
- [Renato e Seus Blue Caps](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/renato-e-seus-blue-caps.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1959 · tier A (Giant). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê. "Menina Linda", "Feche os Olhos".
- [Os Incríveis](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/os-incriveis.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1962 · tier A (Giant). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê. "Era Um Garoto Que Como Eu Amava os Beatles e os Rolling Stones".
- [Wanderléa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/wanderlea.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · debut 1963 · tier A (Giant). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê. Jovem Guarda's "Ternurinha".
- [Jerry Adriani](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jerry-adriani.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1964 · tier A (Giant). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê. Jovem Guarda's romantic idol.
- [Ronnie Von](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ronnie-von.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1966 · tier A (Giant). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê, Psychedelic rock. The "Prince"; "A Máquina Voadora" (1970) is a psychedelic cult record.
- [Fábio Jr.](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/fabio-jr.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1969 · tier A (Giant). Pop rock. Romantic ballads since the 1970s.
- [Baby do Brasil](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/baby-do-brasil.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1970 · tier A (Giant). Psychedelic rock. From Novos Baianos to "Menino do Rio".
- [Ritchie](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ritchie.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1972 · tier A (Giant). Post-punk / new wave. An Englishman based in Brazil; "Menina Veneno" (1983).
- [Lobão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/lobao.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1974 · tier A (Giant). BRock (1980s), Post-punk / new wave. Blitz's drummer, then solo: "Vida Bandida", "Me Chama".
- [Lulu Santos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/lulu-santos.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1974 · tier A (Giant). Pop rock, BRock (1980s). Pop-rock guitarist and songwriter since the 1980s; "Tempos Modernos", "Toda Forma de Amor".
- [Marina Lima](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/marina-lima.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1977 · tier A (Giant). Pop rock. "Fullgás" (1984) opened room for women in pop rock.
- [Camisa de Vênus](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/camisa-de-venus.html): Band · Bahia · debut 1980 · tier A (Giant). Punk, Comic rock. Raw, provocative rock, acid lyrics and Marcelo Nova's persona.
- [Roupa Nova](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/roupa-nova.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1980 · tier A (Giant). Pop rock. Soap-opera soft rock: "Anjo", "Dona", "Whisky a Go-Go".
- [Frejat](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/frejat.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1981 · tier A (Giant). Pop rock. Barão Vermelho's guitarist; solo with "Segredos" and "Amor pra Recomeçar".
- [Ira!](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ira.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1981 · tier A (Giant). BRock (1980s), Post-punk / new wave. São Paulo post-punk with angular riffs and urban lyrics; 1980s classics and a return to the stage.
- [Kid Abelha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/kid-abelha.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1981 · tier A (Giant). BRock (1980s), Pop rock. Pop-rock of catchy melodies and Paula Toller's voice; millions of records sold.
- [Ultraje a Rigor](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ultraje-a-rigor.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1981 · tier A (Giant). BRock (1980s), Punk, Comic rock. Humour, guitars and social critique, with "Inútil"; landmarks for the Diretas Já generation.
- [Capital Inicial](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/capital-inicial.html): Band · Federal District (Brasília) · debut 1982 · tier A (Giant). BRock (1980s), Post-punk / new wave, Brasília rock. Turned Brasília post-punk into a mass language; born from the ashes of Aborto Elétrico.
- [Nando Reis](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nando-reis.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1982 · tier A (Giant). Pop rock. Titãs bassist and hit songwriter for Cássia Eller, Skank and Marisa Monte.
- [RPM](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/rpm.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1983 · tier A (Giant). BRock (1980s), Post-punk / new wave. Synthesizers and "Rádio Pirata ao Vivo", one of the best-selling records of Brazilian rock.
- [Mundo Livre S/A](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mundo-livre-s-a.html): Band · Pernambuco · debut 1984 · tier A (Giant). Manguebeat. Fred Zero Quatro; "Samba Esquema Noise" (1994).
- [Raimundos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/raimundos.html): Band · Federal District (Brasília) · debut 1987 · tier A (Giant). Hardcore, Punk, Comic rock. Hardcore with forró grooves and humour; a trail of hits in the 1990s.
- [Rosa de Saron](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/rosa-de-saron.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1988 · tier A (Giant). Christian rock. Catholic rock: "Sem Você", "Mire as Estrelas".
- [Mamonas Assassinas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mamonas-assassinas.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1989 · tier A (Giant). Comic rock. A one-album phenomenon (1995), humour and millions of copies; the 1996 tragedy ended the story.
- [Cássia Eller](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cassia-eller.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1990 · tier A (Giant). Alternative rock, Festival-era MPB. One of the greatest voices of 1990s Brazilian rock: "Malandragem", "O Segundo Sol".
- [Angra](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/angra.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1991 · tier A (Giant). Heavy and power metal. High-technique power/prog with classical influences; concept albums and a strong following in Europe and Japan.
- [Skank](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/skank.html): Band · Minas Gerais · debut 1991 · tier A (Giant). Pop rock, Ska / reggae rock. From ska to sophisticated pop, a constant presence on radio and in stadiums for three decades.
- [Pato Fu](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/pato-fu.html): Band · Minas Gerais · debut 1992 · tier A (Giant). Pop rock, Alternative rock. With "Música de Brinquedo" it showed a playful concept can reach the top.
- [Jota Quest](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jota-quest.html): Band · Minas Gerais · debut 1993 · tier A (Giant). Pop rock. Pop, funk and soul with a live-band feel; a continuous radio presence since the 1990s.
- [O Rappa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/o-rappa.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1993 · tier A (Giant). Rap rock / nu metal, National reggae. Rock, reggae, funk, hip-hop and samba in urban chronicles; "Lado B Lado A" is the landmark.
- [Planet Hemp](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/planet-hemp.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1993 · tier A (Giant). Rap rock / nu metal. Rap-rock with cannabis-legalization activism; faced arrest and censorship in 1997.
- [CPM 22](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cpm-22.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1995 · tier A (Giant). Hardcore, Pop punk. Took melodic hardcore to the mass public; Latin Grammy for Best Brazilian Rock Album in 2008.
- [Los Hermanos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/los-hermanos.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1997 · tier A (Giant). Indie rock, Alternative rock. From teen hits to sophisticated arrangements; "Ventura" influenced far beyond indie.
- [Pitty](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/pitty.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1997 · tier A (Giant). Alternative rock, Hardcore. With "Admirável Chip Novo" (2003) she put guitars and a female voice back at the centre of pop-rock.
- [Soulfly](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/soulfly.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1997 · tier A (Giant). Thrash, death and black metal. Max Cavalera's project after Sepultura; based in the US.
- [NX Zero](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nx-zero.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 2001 · tier A (Giant). Emo, Hardcore. Cemented emo/hardcore in the 2000s mainstream, with awards and platinum records.
- [CSS](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/css.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 2003 · tier A (Giant). Indie rock, Electronics and funk. Cansei de Ser Sexy: indie-electro in English with international success.
- [Vitor Kley](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/vitor-kley.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 2009 · tier A (Giant). Pop rock. "O Sol" (2018), "Adrenalizou".
- [Anavitória](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/anavitoria.html): Duo · Tocantins · debut 2014 · tier A (Giant). Pop rock, New MPB. A voice-and-guitar duo: "Trevo (Tu)", "Fica".
- [Melim](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/melim.html): Group · Rio de Janeiro · debut 2016 · tier A (Giant). Pop rock, Alternative pop. A sibling trio; "Meu Abrigo", "Ouvi Dizer".
- [Jovem Dionisio](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jovem-dionisio.html): Band · Paraná · debut 2019 · tier A (Giant). Indie rock, Pop rock. "Acorda Pedrinho" (2022) was one of the country's biggest viral hits.
- [Arnaldo Baptista](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/arnaldo-baptista.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier A (Giant). Psychedelic rock. Former Mutantes member, author of the cult album "Lóki?" (1974).
- [Betinho e Seu Conjunto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/betinho-e-seu-conjunto.html): Group · debut 1954 · tier B (Reference). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê. Recorded "Neurastênico" (1954), one of the first Brazilian rock songs.
- [Golden Boys](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/golden-boys.html): Group · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1958 · tier B (Reference). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê. "Alguém na Multidão", "Andança".
- [The Blue Jean Rockers](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/the-blue-jean-rockers.html): Band · debut 1958 · tier B (Reference). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê. A pioneering rock'n'roll group in Brazil.
- [Ed Wilson](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ed-wilson.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1960 · tier B (Reference). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê. "Telefonema", "Biquini de Bolinha Amarelinha".
- [A Bolha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/a-bolha.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1965 · tier B (Reference). Psychedelic rock, Hard rock. 1970s psychedelia and hard rock.
- [Os Baobás](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/os-baobas.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1965 · tier B (Reference). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê, Garage rock. Jovem Guarda garage: "Pintada de Preto".
- [Made in Brazil](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/made-in-brazil.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1967 · tier B (Reference). Hard rock. A São Paulo rock legend, long-lived and powerful on stage.
- [Raulzito e os Panteras](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/raulzito-e-os-panteras.html): Band · Bahia · debut 1967 · tier B (Reference). Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê. Raul Seixas's first recording; an origin point of late-1960s Brazilian rock.
- [O Terço](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/o-terco.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1968 · tier B (Reference). Progressive rock, Psychedelic rock. A pillar of 1970s prog: psychedelia, rural rock and "Criaturas da Noite".
- [Ave Sangria](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ave-sangria.html): Band · Pernambuco · debut 1969 · tier B (Reference). Psychedelic rock. 1970s psychedelia from Pernambuco.
- [Módulo 1000](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/modulo-1000.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1969 · tier B (Reference). Psychedelic rock. "Não Fale com Paredes" (1972), a psychedelic cult record.
- [Pholhas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/pholhas.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1969 · tier B (Reference). Progressive rock. Progressive rock/power pop in English, with "My Mistake".
- [Som Imaginário](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/som-imaginario.html): Band · Minas Gerais · debut 1970 · tier B (Reference). Progressive rock, Clube da Esquina. Milton Nascimento's band; "Feira Moderna".
- [O Peso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/o-peso.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1971 · tier B (Reference). Hard rock, Psychedelic rock. Pioneering hard rock.
- [Light Reflections](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/light-reflections.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1972 · tier B (Reference). Pop rock. 1970s soft rock in English.
- [Casa das Máquinas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/casa-das-maquinas.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1973 · tier B (Reference). Progressive rock, Hard rock. A 1970s pillar, from hard rock to prog; reunited after decades.
- [Bacamarte](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bacamarte.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1974 · tier B (Reference). Progressive rock. "Depois do Fim" (1983), a Brazilian prog classic.
- [Bixo da Seda](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bixo-da-seda.html): Band · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1976 · tier B (Reference). Progressive rock, Gaúcho rock. 1970s prog from Rio Grande do Sul.
- [A Cor do Som](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/a-cor-do-som.html): Band · Bahia · debut 1977 · tier B (Reference). Psychedelic rock. Rock with frevo, baião and choro, born around Novos Baianos.
- [Patrulha do Espaço](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/patrulha-do-espaco.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1977 · tier B (Reference). Hard rock, Progressive rock. Hard/prog with cult albums and the "Columbia" riff.
- [Aborto Elétrico](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/aborto-eletrico.html): Band · Federal District (Brasília) · debut 1978 · tier B (Reference). Punk, Brasília rock. The origin of Legião Urbana and Capital Inicial: short-lived, hugely influential.
- [Metrô](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/metro.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1978 · tier B (Reference). Post-punk / new wave. São Paulo new wave with Virginie Boutaud: "Beat Acelerado".
- [Cólera](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/colera.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1979 · tier B (Reference). Punk. A symbol of São Paulo punk/hardcore, militant stance and DIY practice.
- [João Penca e Seus Miquinhos Amestrados](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/joao-penca-e-seus-miquinhos-amestrados.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1980 · tier B (Reference). Comic rock. Comic rockabilly of the 1980s.
- [Marcelo Nova](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/marcelo-nova.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1980 · tier B (Reference). Punk, Comic rock. Camisa de Vênus's voice; Raul Seixas's partner in 1989.
- [Blitz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/blitz.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1981 · tier B (Reference). BRock (1980s), Post-punk / new wave. Set off the BRock boom in the early 1980s, with theatre, humour and hits.
- [Inocentes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/inocentes.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1981 · tier B (Reference). Punk. One of the foundations of São Paulo punk, with a long career and influence on dozens of bands.
- [Plebe Rude](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/plebe-rude.html): Band · Federal District (Brasília) · debut 1981 · tier B (Reference). Post-punk / new wave, Brasília rock. A key name of Brasília's BRock: post-punk and socio-political lyrics.
- [Ratos de Porão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ratos-de-porao.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1981 · tier B (Reference). Hardcore, Punk, Thrash, death and black metal. Pioneers of hardcore/crossover in Brazil, opening the way for the national extreme-metal scene.
- [Voluntários da Pátria](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/voluntarios-da-patria.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1981 · tier B (Reference). Post-punk / new wave. The first Brazilian post-punk with a clear aesthetic, in São Paulo.
- [Vulcano](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/vulcano.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1981 · tier B (Reference). Thrash, death and black metal. A pioneer of Brazilian extreme metal.
- [Garotos Podres](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/garotos-podres.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1982 · tier B (Reference). Punk. Cheeky, political punk, with "Mais Podres do que Nunca" and "Papai Noel, Velho Batuta".
- [Stress](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/stress.html): Band · Pará · debut 1982 · tier B (Reference). Heavy and power metal. From Belém; in 1982 it recorded Brazil's first heavy metal LP.
- [Dr. Silvana & Cia.](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dr-silvana-e-cia.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1983 · tier B (Reference). Comic rock. "Serão Extra", "Taca a Mãe pra Ver se Quica".
- [Korzus](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/korzus.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1983 · tier B (Reference). Thrash, death and black metal. A veteran of São Paulo thrash, on historic compilations such as "SP Metal II".
- [Leviaethan](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/leviaethan.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1983 · tier B (Reference). Thrash, death and black metal. 1980s thrash.
- [Os Replicantes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/os-replicantes.html): Band · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1983 · tier B (Reference). Punk, Gaúcho rock. Irreverent punk joining cinema and counterculture with acid humour.
- [Zero](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/zero.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1983 · tier B (Reference). Post-punk / new wave. Post-punk with Guilherme Isnard: "Agora Eu Sei", "Formosa".
- [Lobão & Os Ronaldos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/lobao-e-os-ronaldos.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1984 · tier B (Reference). BRock (1980s). The project behind the hit "Me Chama", which helped shape 1980s rock.
- [Supla](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/supla.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1984 · tier B (Reference). Punk, Alternative rock. Punk and rock with a media persona: "Garota de Berlim", "Green Hair".
- [Attomica](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/attomica.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1985 · tier B (Reference). Thrash, death and black metal. 1980s thrash.
- [Biquini Cavadão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/biquini-cavadao.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1985 · tier B (Reference). BRock (1980s), Pop rock. A veteran of "Vento Ventania" and "Janaína", still on big stages; now called Biquini.
- [DeFalla](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/defalla.html): Band · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1985 · tier B (Reference). Post-punk / new wave, Fock. A Porto Alegre rock band that moved from new wave to funk carioca and Miami bass: "Popozuda Rock 'n' Roll".
- [Golpe de Estado](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/golpe-de-estado.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1985 · tier B (Reference). Hard rock. 1980s São Paulo hard rock.
- [Sarcófago](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sarcofago.html): Band · Minas Gerais · debut 1985 · tier B (Reference). Thrash, death and black metal. Seminal in Brazilian black/death metal, with "INRI" and "The Laws of Scourge".
- [Violeta de Outono](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/violeta-de-outono.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1985 · tier B (Reference). Psychedelic rock, Shoegaze. São Paulo psychedelia and post-punk since the 1980s.
- [Viper](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/viper.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1985 · tier B (Reference). Heavy and power metal. A pillar of Brazilian heavy/power metal; it revealed Andre Matos in the late 1980s.
- [Inimigos do Rei](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/inimigos-do-rei.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1986 · tier B (Reference). Comic rock. "Adelaide", "Uma Barata Chamada Kafka".
- [Nenhum de Nós](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nenhum-de-nos.html): Band · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1986 · tier B (Reference). Pop rock, Gaúcho rock. Pop/rock from Rio Grande do Sul with strong melodies, "Camila, Camila" and "O Astronauta de Mármore".
- [Os Cascavelletes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/os-cascavelletes.html): Band · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1986 · tier B (Reference). Comic rock, Gaúcho rock. Icons of southern "porn-rock", irony and controversy.
- [Velhas Virgens](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/velhas-virgens.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1986 · tier B (Reference). Comic rock. Independent and long-lived, adult humour and bar rock with a loyal crowd.
- [Headhunter D.C.](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/headhunter-d-c.html): Band · Bahia · debut 1987 · tier B (Reference). Thrash, death and black metal. Death metal from Bahia.
- [Oficina G3](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/oficina-g3.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1987 · tier B (Reference). Christian rock, Heavy and power metal. A pioneer of Christian and progressive metal in Brazil.
- [Catedral](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/catedral.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1988 · tier B (Reference). Christian rock. Christian pop rock.
- [Devotos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/devotos.html): Band · Pernambuco · debut 1988 · tier B (Reference). Hardcore, Manguebeat. Hardcore from Alto José do Pinho, Recife.
- [Anjos da Noite](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/anjos-da-noite.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1989 · tier B (Reference). Hard rock. 1990s hard/glam.
- [Lan Lan](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/lan-lan.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1989 · tier B (Reference). Pop rock. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Song.
- [Resgate](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/resgate.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1989 · tier B (Reference). Christian rock. Christian rock since the 1980s.
- [Virna Lisi](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/virna-lisi.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1989 · tier B (Reference). Comic rock. São Paulo comic rock.
- [Ajna](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ajna.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1990 · tier B (Reference). Heavy and power metal. Heavy/thrash in English.
- [Gritando HC](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/gritando-hc.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1990 · tier B (Reference). Hardcore. "Velho Punk".
- [Júpiter Maçã](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jupiter-maca.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1990 · tier B (Reference). Psychedelic rock, Gaúcho rock. "A Sétima Efervescência" (1997), cult psychedelia.

### Sertanejo (111)

- [Tonico & Tinoco](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tonico-e-tinoco.html): Duo · São Paulo · debut 1942 · tier S (Legend). Caipira / roots. The longest-lived and best-selling caipira duo: "Tristeza do Jeca", "Chico Mineiro".
- [Tião Carreiro & Pardinho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tiao-carreiro-e-pardinho.html): Duo · São Paulo · debut 1961 · tier S (Legend). Caipira / roots. Creators of the pagode de viola: "Pagode em Brasília", "Rei do Gado".
- [Chitãozinho & Xororó](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/chitaozinho-e-xororo.html): Duo · Paraná · debut 1969 · tier S (Legend). Romantic sertanejo, Caipira / roots. Modernized sertanejo with "Fio de Cabelo" (1982) and "Evidências"; opened the genre to pop.
- [Leandro & Leonardo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/leandro-e-leonardo.html): Duo · Goiás · debut 1983 · tier S (Legend). Romantic sertanejo. "Entre Tapas e Beijos", "Pense em Mim"; Leandro's death in 1998 stopped the country.
- [Zezé Di Camargo & Luciano](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/zeze-di-camargo-e-luciano.html): Duo · Goiás · debut 1991 · tier S (Legend). Romantic sertanejo. "É o Amor" (1991) sold millions; film "2 Filhos de Francisco".
- [Bruno & Marrone](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bruno-e-marrone.html): Duo · Goiás · debut 1994 · tier S (Legend). Romantic sertanejo. "Dormi na Praça", "Vida Vazia"; the longest-running romantic duo.
- [Jorge & Mateus](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jorge-e-mateus.html): Duo · Goiás · debut 2007 · tier S (Legend). Sertanejo universitário. The most streamed duo of sertanejo universitário: "Pode Chorar", "Sosseguei".
- [Gusttavo Lima](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/gusttavo-lima.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · debut 2009 · tier S (Legend). Sertanejo universitário. "Balada (Tchê Tcherere Tchê Tchê)" (2011); the "Ambassador".
- [Luan Santana](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/luan-santana.html): Solo · Mato Grosso do Sul · debut 2009 · tier S (Legend). Sertanejo universitário, Alternative pop. "Meteoro", "Escreve Aí", "Morena"; sertanejo's teen idol.
- [Michel Teló](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/michel-telo.html): Solo · Paraná · debut 2009 · tier S (Legend). Sertanejo universitário. "Ai Se Eu Te Pego" (2011) topped charts in over 20 countries.
- [Henrique & Juliano](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/henrique-e-juliano.html): Duo · Tocantins · debut 2011 · tier S (Legend). Sertanejo universitário. "Cuida Bem Dela", "Vidinha de Balada".
- [Marília Mendonça](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/marilia-mendonca.html): Solo · Goiás · debut 2015 · tier S (Legend). Feminejo. The "queen of sofrência": "Infiel", "Todos os Cantos"; she died in a plane crash in 2021.
- [Ana Castela](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ana-castela.html): Solo · Mato Grosso do Sul · debut 2021 · tier S (Legend). Agronejo. The "Boiadeira": "Pipoco", "Nosso Quadro"; the agronejo of the 2020s.
- [Maiara & Maraisa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/maiara-e-maraisa.html): Duo · Mato Grosso · tier S (Legend). Feminejo. "10%", "Medo Bobo"; with Marília, the "Patroas".
- [Cornélio Pires](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cornelio-pires.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1929 · tier A (Giant). Caipira / roots. The first to record caipira music, in 1929.
- [Alvarenga & Ranchinho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/alvarenga-e-ranchinho.html): Duo · São Paulo · debut 1936 · tier A (Giant). Caipira / roots. A humorous caipira duo of the 1930s and 1940s.
- [Zé Carreiro & Carreirinho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ze-carreiro-e-carreirinho.html): Duo · São Paulo · debut 1950 · tier A (Giant). Caipira / roots. Masters of cururu and the moda de viola.
- [Cascatinha & Inhana](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cascatinha-e-inhana.html): Duo · São Paulo · debut 1951 · tier A (Giant). Caipira / roots. Caipira music's romantic duo: "Índia".
- [Inezita Barroso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/inezita-barroso.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1951 · tier A (Giant). Caipira / roots. Guardian of caipira music; hosted "Viola, Minha Viola" on TV Cultura for decades.
- [Sérgio Reis](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sergio-reis.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1967 · tier A (Giant). Caipira / roots, Jovem Guarda / iê-iê-iê. From Jovem Guarda to the viola: "Panela Velha", "Menino da Porteira".
- [Renato Teixeira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/renato-teixeira.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1969 · tier A (Giant). Caipira / roots, Festival-era MPB. "Romaria", "Tocando em Frente".
- [Milionário & José Rico](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/milionario-e-jose-rico.html): Duo · São Paulo · debut 1972 · tier A (Giant). Romantic sertanejo. "Estrada da Vida", a highway classic.
- [Trio Parada Dura](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/trio-parada-dura.html): Band · Minas Gerais · debut 1973 · tier A (Giant). Romantic sertanejo. "Blusa Vermelha", "Castelo de Amor".
- [Almir Sater](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/almir-sater.html): Solo · Mato Grosso do Sul · debut 1981 · tier A (Giant). Caipira / roots. Viola and "Tocando em Frente", "Chalana".
- [João Paulo & Daniel](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/joao-paulo-e-daniel.html): Duo · São Paulo · debut 1985 · tier A (Giant). Romantic sertanejo. "Estou Apaixonado"; Daniel went solo after 1997.
- [Roberta Miranda](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/roberta-miranda.html): Solo · Paraíba · debut 1986 · tier A (Giant). Romantic sertanejo. The "queen of sertanejo": "Majestade, o Sabiá", "Vá com Deus".
- [Rick & Renner](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/rick-e-renner.html): Duo · Goiás · debut 1991 · tier A (Giant). Romantic sertanejo. "Ela É Demais", "Filha".
- [Daniel](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/daniel.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1997 · tier A (Giant). Romantic sertanejo. Formerly of João Paulo & Daniel; "Adoro Amar Você"; a coach on The Voice Brasil.
- [Leonardo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/leonardo.html): Solo · Goiás · debut 1998 · tier A (Giant). Romantic sertanejo. Solo career after Leandro's death: "Pense em Mim", "Deixaria Tudo".
- [Victor & Leo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/victor-e-leo.html): Duo · Minas Gerais · debut 2002 · tier A (Giant). Sertanejo universitário. "Fada", "Borboletas"; romantic sertanejo universitário.
- [Eduardo Costa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/eduardo-costa.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · debut 2003 · tier A (Giant). Sertanejo universitário. "Ilegal, Imoral ou Engorda", "Enamorado".
- [Paula Fernandes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/paula-fernandes.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · debut 2005 · tier A (Giant). Sertanejo universitário. "Pássaro de Fogo", "Não Precisa".

- [Matheus & Kauan](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/matheus-e-kauan.html): Duo · Goiás · debut 2012 · tier A (Giant). Sertanejo universitário. "Que Sorte a Nossa".

- [Diego & Victor Hugo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/diego-e-victor-hugo.html): Duo · Goiás · debut 2014 · tier A (Giant). Sertanejo universitário. 2010s sertanejo.

### Brazilian Funk (121)

- [DJ Marlboro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dj-marlboro.html): DJ · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1989 · tier S (Legend). Funk melody. The "father of funk": "Funk Brasil" (1989) introduced funk carioca in Portuguese.

- [Ludmilla](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ludmilla.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 2012 · tier S (Legend). Funk pop, Contemporary pop, Pagode. From MC Beyoncé to "Cheguei", "Din Din Din" and the pagode project "Numanice"; a Latin Grammy.
- [MC Ryan SP](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mc-ryan-sp.html): MC · São Paulo · debut 2019 · tier S (Legend). Mandelão / bruxaria, Funk pop. One of the most streamed names of São Paulo funk in the 2020s.

### Rap and Hip-Hop (120)

- [Racionais MC's](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/racionais-mc-s.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1988 · tier S (Legend). Rap nacional. Mano Brown, Ice Blue, Edi Rock and KL Jay; "Sobrevivendo no Inferno" (1997) is the most important Brazilian rap album.
- [Criolo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/criolo.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1989 · tier S (Legend). Rap nacional, New MPB. "Nó na Orelha" (2011) joined rap, samba and afrobeat: "Não Existe Amor em SP".
- [Emicida](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/emicida.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 2008 · tier S (Legend). Rap nacional. From rap battles to the Laboratório Fantasma label and "AmarElo" (2019).
- [Matuê](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/matue.html): Solo · Ceará · debut 2017 · tier S (Legend). Brazilian trap. The name of Brazilian trap: "Máquina do Tempo" (2020) broke Spotify Brazil records; 30PRAUM label.
- [Thaíde & DJ Hum](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/thaide-e-dj-hum.html): Duo · São Paulo · debut 1988 · tier A (Giant). Rap nacional. São Paulo rap pioneers: "Corpo Fechado", "Senhor Tempo Bom".
- [Gabriel o Pensador](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/gabriel-o-pensador.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1992 · tier A (Giant). Rap nacional. "Tô Feliz (Matei o Presidente)", "Lôraburra", "Cachimbo da Paz".
- [Dina Di](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dina-di.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1993 · tier A (Giant). Rap nacional. Visão de Rua's singer, considered the first successful woman in Brazilian rap; "A Noiva de Chuck".
- [Marcelo D2](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/marcelo-d2.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1993 · tier A (Giant). Rap nacional, Samba-rock. From Planet Hemp to the samba-rap of "À Procura da Batida Perfeita" (2003).
- [Negra Li](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/negra-li.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1996 · tier A (Giant). Rap nacional. Started in RZO and went solo; "Não É Sério" with Charlie Brown Jr.
- [Sabotage](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sabotage.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 2000 · tier A (Giant). Rap nacional. "Rap É Compromisso" (2000); murdered in 2003, he became a legend.
- [Filipe Ret](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/filipe-ret.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 2008 · tier A (Giant). Rap nacional, Brazilian trap. Rio rap with a bossa touch: "Caminho".
