- [Illusionize](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/illusionize.html): DJ · tier B (Reference). Brazilian bass. Brazilian bass DJ and producer.
- [L_cio](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/l-cio.html): DJ · tier B (Reference). House and techno. House and techno DJ and producer.
- [Liu](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/liu.html): DJ · tier B (Reference). Brazilian bass. Brazilian bass DJ and producer.
- [Mau Mau](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mau-mau.html): DJ · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). House and techno. A pioneering DJ of São Paulo's electronic scene.
- [Mixhell](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mixhell.html): Duo · tier B (Reference). House and techno. An electronic music duo.
- [Mochakk](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mochakk.html): DJ · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). House and techno. House from Sorocaba, touring worldwide.
- [Renato Cohen](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/renato-cohen.html): DJ · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). House and techno. São Paulo techno DJ and producer.
- [Renato Ratier](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/renato-ratier.html): DJ · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). House and techno. DJ and founder of the D-Edge club in São Paulo.
- [Rica Amaral](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/rica-amaral.html): DJ · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Psytrance. A psytrance DJ of Brazil's big festivals.
- [Teto Preto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/teto-preto.html): Band · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). House and techno. São Paulo group between techno and performance.
- [Victor Lou](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/victor-lou.html): DJ · tier B (Reference). Brazilian bass. Brazilian bass DJ and producer.
- [Victor Ruiz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/victor-ruiz.html): DJ · tier B (Reference). House and techno. Techno DJ and producer.
- [Wrecked Machines](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/wrecked-machines.html): Duo · tier B (Reference). Psytrance. A Brazilian psytrance duo.
- [Zerb](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/zerb.html): DJ · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian bass. "Mwaki" (2023) entered the global charts.

### Brazilian Reggae (18)

- [Cidade Negra](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cidade-negra.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1986 · tier S (Legend). National reggae. Brazil's most successful reggae: "Onde Você Mora?", "Girassol", "A Sombra da Maldade".
- [Natiruts](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/natiruts.html): Band · Federal District (Brasília) · debut 1996 · tier S (Legend). National reggae. Alexandre Carlo; "Liberdade pra Dentro da Cabeça", "Quero Ser Feliz Também".
- [Tribo de Jah](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tribo-de-jah.html): Band · Maranhão · debut 1986 · tier A (Giant). Maranhão reggae. Reggae from São Luís, the "Brazilian Jamaica".
- [Edson Gomes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/edson-gomes.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1988 · tier A (Giant). National reggae. Reggae from Cachoeira (BA): "Malandrinha".
- [Planta & Raiz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/planta-e-raiz.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1998 · tier A (Giant). National reggae. "Com Certeza", "Aquele Lugar".
- [Armandinho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/armandinho.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 2001 · tier A (Giant). National reggae. Reggae from Rio Grande do Sul: "Analua", "Outra Vida".
- [Maneva](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/maneva.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 2005 · tier A (Giant). National reggae. "Pisando Descalço", "Saudades do Tempo".
- [Chimarruts](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/chimarruts.html): Band · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1999 · tier B (Reference). National reggae. "Do Lado de Cá".
- [Ponto de Equilíbrio](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ponto-de-equilibrio.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1999 · tier B (Reference). National reggae. Rio reggae.
- [Adão Negro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/adao-negro.html): Band · Bahia · tier B (Reference). National reggae. Bahian reggae band.
- [Alma Djem](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/alma-djem.html): Band · tier B (Reference). National reggae. Brazilian pop reggae.
- [Diamba](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/diamba.html): Band · tier B (Reference). National reggae. A reggae band.
- [Leões de Israel](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/leoes-de-israel.html): Band · tier B (Reference). National reggae. A reggae band.
- [Mato Seco](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mato-seco.html): Band · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). National reggae. São Paulo reggae band.
- [Mosiah](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mosiah.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). National reggae. Reggae singer.
- [Nengo Vieira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nengo-vieira.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). National reggae. Reggae singer.
- [Onze:20](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/onze-20.html): Band · tier B (Reference). National reggae. Rio pop reggae of the 2010s.
- [Ras Bernardo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ras-bernardo.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). National reggae. Cidade Negra's first singer.

### Soul and Black Music (25)

- [Tim Maia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tim-maia.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1970 · tier S (Legend). Brazilian soul. The "Síndico": invented Brazilian soul; "Primavera", "Gostava Tanto de Você", "Me Dê Motivo".
- [Banda Black Rio](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/banda-black-rio.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1976 · tier S (Legend). Black Rio, Samba-soul, Samba-funk. Instrumental funk from the Black Rio movement: "Maria Fumaça".
- [Wilson Simonal](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/wilson-simonal.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1961 · tier A (Giant). Brazilian soul, Samba-jazz, Sambalanço, Samba-soul. The "pilantragem" swing: "Mamãe Passou Açúcar em Mim", "País Tropical".
- [Cassiano](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cassiano.html): Solo · Paraíba · debut 1970 · tier A (Giant). Brazilian soul. "Primavera" (composer), "A Lua e Eu".
- [Toni Tornado](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/toni-tornado.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1970 · tier A (Giant). Black Rio. "BR-3" won the 1970 FIC; the Brazilian James Brown.
- [Hyldon](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/hyldon.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1975 · tier A (Giant). Brazilian soul. "Na Rua, na Chuva, na Fazenda".
- [Gerson King Combo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/gerson-king-combo.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1977 · tier A (Giant). Black Rio. "Mandamentos Black".
- [Sandra de Sá](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sandra-de-sa.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1980 · tier A (Giant). Brazilian soul. "Olhos Coloridos", "Bye Bye Tristeza".
- [Ed Motta](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ed-motta.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1988 · tier A (Giant). Brazilian soul, Brazilian jazz. Tim Maia's nephew; "Manuel", "Colombina"; soul and AOR jazz.
- [Liniker](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/liniker.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 2015 · tier A (Giant). Neo-soul and R&B, New MPB. Soul and MPB; the first trans artist to win a Latin Grammy, for "Indigo Borboleta Anil".
- [Carlos Dafé](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/carlos-dafe.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1977 · tier B (Reference). Brazilian soul. "Pra Que Vou Recordar".
- [Paula Lima](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/paula-lima.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1999 · tier B (Reference). Neo-soul and R&B. São Paulo soul and samba-funk.
- [Luedji Luna](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/luedji-luna.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 2017 · tier B (Reference). Neo-soul and R&B, New MPB. "Bom Mesmo É Estar Debaixo D'Água" (2020).
- [Xênia França](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/xenia-franca.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 2017 · tier B (Reference). Neo-soul and R&B. Formerly of Aláfia; the album "Xenia" (2017).
- [Claudia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/claudia.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian soul. Singer of "Deixa Eu Dizer" (1973).
- [Cláudio Zoli](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/claudio-zoli.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Brazilian soul. Former Brylho singer ("Noite do Prazer") and a name in Rio soul.
- [Di Melo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/di-melo.html): Solo · Pernambuco · tier B (Reference). Brazilian soul. Soul and funk with psychedelia; his debut album (1975) became a cult record.
- [Ivan Barreto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/ivan-barreto.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Brazilian soul. A singer from Uberlândia (Minas Gerais) who won The Voice Brasil 2023 on Lulu Santos's team.
- [Keilla Júnia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/keilla-junia.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Neo-soul and R&B. A singer from Matozinhos (Minas Gerais) who won The Voice Brasil 2022, aged 18, on Michel Teló's team.
- [Léo Maia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/leo-maia.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Brazilian soul. A soul singer and guitarist, Tim Maia's adopted son.
- [Max de Castro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/max-de-castro.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Brazilian soul. A soul and samba-rock multi-instrumentalist and producer, Wilson Simonal's son.
- [Mylena Jardim](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mylena-jardim.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Neo-soul and R&B. An R&B singer from Belo Horizonte who won The Voice Brasil 2016, aged 17, on Michel Teló's team.
- [Tony Gordon](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tony-gordon.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian soul. Won The Voice Brasil 2019, aged 53, on Michel Teló's team: the oldest winner in the whole The Voice franchise.
- [Trio Ternura](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/trio-ternura.html): Group · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Brazilian soul. Vocal trio of "Sempre Existe Alguém" (1971).
- [Wilson Simoninha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/wilson-simoninha.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Brazilian soul. A singer, songwriter and producer, Wilson Simonal's son.

### Jazz and Instrumental (54)

- [Hermeto Pascoal](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/hermeto-pascoal.html): Solo · Alagoas · debut 1958 · tier S (Legend). Brazilian jazz. The "Sorcerer": a multi-instrumentalist recorded by Miles Davis; "Bebê", "Chorinho pra Ele".
- [Airto Moreira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/airto-moreira.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1964 · tier S (Legend). Brazilian jazz. Drummer and percussionist with Miles Davis, Weather Report and Return to Forever.
- [Naná Vasconcelos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nana-vasconcelos.html): Solo · Pernambuco · debut 1967 · tier S (Legend). Brazilian jazz. Berimbau and percussion with Pat Metheny and Egberto; eight-time best percussionist in Down Beat.
- [Egberto Gismonti](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/egberto-gismonti.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1969 · tier S (Legend). Brazilian jazz. Guitar and piano on ECM: "Dança das Cabeças", "Sol do Meio Dia".
- [Azymuth](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/azymuth.html): Band · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1973 · tier S (Legend). Fusion and jazz-funk. Jazz-funk revered by DJs: "Jazz Carnival", "Light as a Feather".
- [Eumir Deodato](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/eumir-deodato.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1964 · tier A (Giant). Fusion and jazz-funk. "Also Sprach Zarathustra (2001)" won a Grammy in 1974; producer for Kool & the Gang.
- [Flora Purim](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/flora-purim.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1964 · tier A (Giant). Brazilian jazz. Singer of Return to Forever; five Grammy nominations.
- [Moacir Santos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/moacir-santos.html): Solo · Pernambuco · debut 1965 · tier A (Giant). Brazilian jazz. "Coisas" (1965), a masterpiece of Brazilian jazz.
- [Quarteto Novo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/quarteto-novo.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1967 · tier A (Giant). Brazilian jazz. Hermeto, Airto, Heraldo do Monte and Théo de Barros: baião in jazz.
- [Tania Maria](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tania-maria.html): Solo · Maranhão · debut 1970 · tier A (Giant). Brazilian jazz. Piano and voice between samba and jazz, based in Europe and the US.
- [Uakti](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/uakti.html): Band · Minas Gerais · debut 1978 · tier A (Giant). Brazilian jazz. Invented instruments in PVC and glass; recorded with Philip Glass.
- [Eliane Elias](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/eliane-elias.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1981 · tier A (Giant). Brazilian jazz. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Song and the Latin Grammy for Best Latin Jazz/Jazz Album.
- [Amaro Freitas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/amaro-freitas.html): Solo · Pernambuco · tier A (Giant). Brazilian jazz. Recife pianist who brings frevo and maracatu into jazz.
- [Cesar Camargo Mariano](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cesar-camargo-mariano.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier A (Giant). Brazilian jazz. Pianist and arranger, Elis Regina's partner.
- [Garoto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/garoto.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier A (Giant). Brazilian guitar, Choro. Aníbal Augusto Sardinha, a guitarist who anticipated bossa nova harmony.
- [João Donato](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/joao-donato.html): Solo · Acre · tier A (Giant). Brazilian jazz, Bossa nova. Pianist from Acre, a pioneer of bossa nova and Latin jazz.
- [Laurindo Almeida](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/laurindo-almeida.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier A (Giant). Brazilian guitar. Nominated for a Grammy.
- [Luiz Bonfá](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/luiz-bonfa.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Brazilian guitar, Bossa nova. Guitarist and composer of "Manhã de Carnaval", from the film "Black Orpheus".
- [Raphael Rabello](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/raphael-rabello.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Brazilian guitar, Choro. A virtuoso of the seven-string guitar.
- [Toninho Horta](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/toninho-horta.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier A (Giant). Brazilian jazz, Clube da Esquina. Guitarist and composer of Clube da Esquina, a worldwide guitar reference.
- [Orquestra Afro-Brasileira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-afro-brasileira.html): Collective · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1942 · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Created in 1942 by Abigail Moura, it joined Western horns with Afro-Brazilian percussion; revived in 2021.
- [Dom Um Romão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dom-um-romao.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1960 · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Drummer with Weather Report and Sérgio Mendes.
- [Raul de Souza](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/raul-de-souza.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1965 · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Trombonist in Brazilian and American jazz.
- [Romero Lubambo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/romero-lubambo.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1980 · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best MPB Album.
- [Brasil Jazz Sinfônica](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/brasil-jazz-sinfonica.html): Collective · São Paulo · debut 1989 · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. A 70-piece orchestra created in 1989 by the São Paulo state government, with symphonic arrangements of Brazilian popular music.
- [Banda Mantiqueira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/banda-mantiqueira.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 1991 · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. São Paulo big band.
- [Luciana Souza](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/luciana-souza.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1992 · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Nominated for a Grammy.
- [André Mehmari](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/andre-mehmari.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1995 · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Pianist and composer in jazz and classical music.
- [Brazilian Guitar Quartet](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/brazilian-guitar-quartet.html): Group · debut 1998 · tier B (Reference). Brazilian guitar. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Classical Album.
- [Trio Corrente](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/trio-corrente.html): Band · São Paulo · debut 2001 · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Latin Grammy with Paquito D'Rivera (2014).
- [Orkestra Rumpilezz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orkestra-rumpilezz.html): Collective · Bahia · debut 2006 · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. A percussion and wind orchestra created in 2006 by Letieres Leite; the name joins the candomblé drums (rum, rumpi and lé) with jazz.
- [André Marques](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/andre-marques.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Latin Jazz/Jazz Album.
- [Antonio Loureiro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/antonio-loureiro.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz, New MPB. Minas Gerais multi-instrumentalist and composer.
- [Arismar do Espírito Santo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/arismar-do-espirito-santo.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. A multi-instrumentalist of Brazilian jazz.
- [Chico Pinheiro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/chico-pinheiro.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Guitarist and composer.
- [Cristovão Bastos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cristovao-bastos.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Instrumental Album.
- [Delia Fischer](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/delia-fischer.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best MPB Album.
- [Diego Figueiredo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/diego-figueiredo.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian guitar. Nominated for a Grammy.
- [Dilermando Reis](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/dilermando-reis.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian guitar. Radio-era guitarist, a performer of waltzes and choros.
- [Duofel](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/duofel.html): Duo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian guitar. An acoustic guitar duo.
- [Guga Stroeter](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/guga-stroeter.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Samba/Pagode Album.
- [Heraldo do Monte](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/heraldo-do-monte.html): Solo · Pernambuco · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Guitarist of Quarteto Novo.
- [Itiberê Zwarg](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/itibere-zwarg.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Bassist in Hermeto Pascoal's group.
- [Jovino Santos Neto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jovino-santos-neto.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Pianist and flautist, formerly in Hermeto Pascoal's group.
- [Léa Freire](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/lea-freire.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Flautist and composer.
- [Mauro Senise](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mauro-senise.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best MPB Album and the Latin Grammy for Best Instrumental Album.
- [Nailor Azevedo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nailor-azevedo.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Latin Jazz/Jazz Album.
- [Nelson Ayres](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nelson-ayres.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Pianist, arranger and conductor.
- [Pau Brasil](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/pau-brasil.html): Band · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. São Paulo instrumental group.
- [Rosinha de Valença](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/rosinha-de-valenca.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Brazilian guitar. A guitarist, singer and songwriter from Rio de Janeiro state.
- [Rubem Dantas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/rubem-dantas.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Latin Jazz/Jazz Album.
- [Teco Cardoso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/teco-cardoso.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Saxophonist and flautist.
- [Victor Assis Brasil](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/victor-assis-brasil.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz. Brazilian jazz saxophonist.
- [Wagner Tiso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/wagner-tiso.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Brazilian jazz, Clube da Esquina. Pianist and arranger of Clube da Esquina.

### Classical Music (59)

- [Carlos Gomes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/carlos-gomes.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1861 · tier S (Legend). Romanticism. "O Guarani" (1870) premiered at La Scala in Milan.
- [Heitor Villa-Lobos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/heitor-villa-lobos.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1910 · tier S (Legend). Nationalism. Brazil's greatest composer: "Bachianas Brasileiras", "Choros", "Floresta do Amazonas".
- [Nelson Freire](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nelson-freire.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · debut 1957 · tier S (Legend). Performers, orchestras and choirs. World-renowned pianist; duos with Martha Argerich.
- [Guiomar Novaes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/guiomar-novaes.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1911 · tier A (Giant). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Pianist acclaimed in Paris and New York in the early 20th century.
- [Francisco Mignone](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/francisco-mignone.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1920 · tier A (Giant). Nationalism. "Maracatu de Chico Rei", street-corner waltzes.
- [Bidu Sayão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bidu-sayao.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1926 · tier A (Giant). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Soprano at the Metropolitan Opera from 1937 to 1952.
- [Camargo Guarnieri](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/camargo-guarnieri.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1928 · tier A (Giant). Nationalism. Musical nationalism; symphonies and "Dansa Brasileira".
- [Radamés Gnattali](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/radames-gnattali.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1930 · tier A (Giant). Nationalism, Choro. Between classical and popular; arranger for Rádio Nacional.
- [OSESP](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/osesp.html): Collective · São Paulo · debut 1954 · tier A (Giant). Performers, orchestras and choirs. São Paulo State Symphony; Sala São Paulo; led by John Neschling, Marin Alsop and Thierry Fischer.
- [Orquestra Filarmônica de Minas Gerais](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-filarmonica-de-minas-gerais.html): Collective · Minas Gerais · debut 2008 · tier A (Giant). Performers, orchestras and choirs. A symphony orchestra created in 2008 in Belo Horizonte, conducted by Fabio Mechetti.
- [Isaac Karabtchevsky](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/isaac-karabtchevsky.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier A (Giant). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Classical Album.
- [José Maurício Nunes Garcia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jose-mauricio-nunes-garcia.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Colonial music. Priest and court composer in Rio, the greatest name in Brazilian colonial music.
- [João Carlos Martins](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/joao-carlos-martins.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier A (Giant). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Pianist and conductor, a performer of Bach.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica Brasileira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-brasileira.html): Collective · Rio de Janeiro · tier A (Giant). Performers, orchestras and choirs. OSB, one of the country's most important orchestras, based in central Rio de Janeiro.
- [Orquestra Lira Sanjoanense](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-lira-sanjoanense.html): Collective · Minas Gerais · debut 1776 · tier B (Reference). Colonial music. A São João del-Rei orchestra founded in 1776, cited as one of the oldest active orchestras in the Americas.
- [Alberto Nepomuceno](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/alberto-nepomuceno.html): Solo · Ceará · debut 1880 · tier B (Reference). Romanticism, Nationalism. Father of Brazilian musical nationalism.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica do Recife](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-do-recife.html): Collective · Pernambuco · debut 1930 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Founded in 1930, it is considered Brazil's oldest orchestra in uninterrupted activity.
- [César Guerra-Peixe](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cesar-guerra-peixe.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1940 · tier B (Reference). Nationalism. Researched maracatu and northeastern folklore.
- [Eleazar de Carvalho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/eleazar-de-carvalho.html): Solo · Ceará · debut 1941 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Conductor and teacher of Claudio Abbado and Zubin Mehta at Tanglewood.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica da Paraíba](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-da-paraiba.html): Collective · Paraíba · debut 1945 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. OSPB, founded in 1945 in João Pessoa.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica de Porto Alegre](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-de-porto-alegre.html): Collective · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1950 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. OSPA, founded in 1949 and re-founded as an independent body in 1950.
- [Madrigal Renascentista](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/madrigal-renascentista.html): Collective · Minas Gerais · debut 1956 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. A professional choir founded in 1956 in Belo Horizonte; it sang at the inaugural mass of Brasília.
- [Marlos Nobre](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/marlos-nobre.html): Solo · Pernambuco · debut 1960 · tier B (Reference). Contemporary music. Award-winning contemporary composer.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica Nacional da UFF](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-nacional-da-uff.html): Collective · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1961 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Founded in 1961 by Juscelino Kubitschek to spread Brazilian concert music; part of UFF since 1984.
- [Quinteto Villa-Lobos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/quinteto-villa-lobos.html): Group · debut 1962 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Instrumental Album.
- [Coralusp](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/coralusp.html): Collective · São Paulo · debut 1967 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. The University of São Paulo choir, founded in 1967 by Benito Juarez and José Luiz Visconti.
- [Arnaldo Cohen](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/arnaldo-cohen.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1972 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Pianist based in the US.
- [Orquestra Petrobras Sinfônica](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-petrobras-sinfonica.html): Collective · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1972 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Created in 1972 by conductor Armando Prazeres; Isaac Karabtchevsky is its principal conductor.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica da USP](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-da-usp.html): Collective · São Paulo · debut 1975 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. OSUSP, the University of São Paulo orchestra, founded in 1975.
- [Meninas Cantoras de Petrópolis](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/meninas-cantoras-de-petropolis.html): Collective · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1976 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Founded in 1976, it was considered the first choir made up only of girls.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica do Teatro Nacional Claudio Santoro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-do-teatro-nacional-claudio-santoro.html): Collective · Federal District (Brasília) · debut 1979 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Founded in 1979 in Brasília by conductor and composer Claudio Santoro, after whom it is now named.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica da Bahia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-da-bahia.html): Collective · Bahia · debut 1982 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. OSBA, founded in 1944 and re-founded in 1982; a resident ensemble of Teatro Castro Alves in Salvador.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica do Paraná](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-do-parana.html): Collective · Paraná · debut 1985 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Created in 1985 at Teatro Guaíra in Curitiba.
- [Calíope](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/caliope.html): Collective · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1993 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. A Rio de Janeiro vocal group since 1993; it won the Carlos Gomes Prize for choirs in 2002.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica do Teatro da Paz](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-do-teatro-da-paz.html): Collective · Pará · debut 1996 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Created in 1996 in Belém for the concerts of the Theatro da Paz.
- [Sinfônica Heliópolis](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sinfonica-heliopolis.html): Collective · São Paulo · debut 1996 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. The Instituto Baccarelli orchestra, born in 1996 with students from the Heliópolis community in São Paulo.
- [Amazonas Filarmônica](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/amazonas-filarmonica.html): Collective · Amazonas · debut 1997 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. A Manaus orchestra founded in 1997.
- [Orquestra Ouro Preto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-ouro-preto.html): Collective · Minas Gerais · debut 2000 · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. A Minas Gerais orchestra founded in 2000, conducted by Rodrigo Toffolo.
- [Almeida Prado](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/almeida-prado.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Contemporary music. Composer and pianist, author of the "Cartas Celestes".
- [Antonio Meneses](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/antonio-meneses.html): Solo · Pernambuco · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Cellist from Recife, a member of the Beaux Arts Trio.
- [Canarinhos de Petrópolis](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/canarinhos-de-petropolis.html): Collective · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. A youth choir of the Instituto dos Meninos Cantores de Petrópolis.
- [Clara Sverner](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/clara-sverner.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Classical Album.
- [Coral Ars Nova](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/coral-ars-nova.html): Collective · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. The UFMG choir, described as the country's most awarded.
- [Coral Paulistano Mário de Andrade](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/coral-paulistano-mario-de-andrade.html): Collective · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. The choir of São Paulo's Theatro Municipal, singing a cappella repertoire, above all by 20th-century Brazilian composers.
- [Coro da Osesp](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/coro-da-osesp.html): Collective · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. The symphonic choir of Sala São Paulo; conducted for two decades by Naomi Munakata, it is a national vocal reference.
- [Coro do Theatro Municipal do Rio de Janeiro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/coro-do-theatro-municipal-do-rio-de-janeiro.html): Collective · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. A 95-voice choir for the operas and concerts of Rio de Janeiro's Theatro Municipal.
- [Coro Lírico Municipal de São Paulo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/coro-lirico-municipal-de-sao-paulo.html): Collective · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. An 88-voice opera choir of São Paulo's Theatro Municipal.
- [Débora Halász](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/debora-halasz.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Classical Album.
- [Elsie Houston](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/elsie-houston.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. A Rio soprano who took Brazilian folk songs to the concert halls of Paris and New York.
- [Gilberto Mendes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/gilberto-mendes.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Contemporary music. Composer from Santos, a signatory of the Música Nova manifesto (1963).
- [John Neschling](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/john-neschling.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Classical Album.
- [Lobo de Mesquita](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/lobo-de-mesquita.html): Solo · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Colonial music. Composer and organist of 18th-century sacred music in Minas.
- [Orquestra Experimental de Repertório](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-experimental-de-repertorio.html): Collective · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. OER, a resident ensemble of São Paulo's Theatro Municipal, based at Praça das Artes.
- [Orquestra Ribeiro Bastos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-ribeiro-bastos.html): Collective · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Colonial music. A musical ensemble based in São João del-Rei, Minas Gerais.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica de Minas Gerais](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-de-minas-gerais.html): Collective · Minas Gerais · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. OSMG, the orchestra of the Palácio das Artes in Belo Horizonte.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica do Theatro Municipal do Rio de Janeiro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-do-theatro-municipal-do-rio-de-janeiro.html): Collective · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. The orchestra of the opera seasons at Rio de Janeiro's Theatro Municipal.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica Municipal de Campinas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-municipal-de-campinas.html): Collective · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. The Campinas Symphony, one of the country's biggest orchestras outside a state capital.
- [Orquestra Sinfônica Municipal de São Paulo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/orquestra-sinfonica-municipal-de-sao-paulo.html): Collective · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. OSM, the orchestra of São Paulo's Theatro Municipal, playing opera and concerts.
- [Sonia Rubinsky](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/sonia-rubinsky.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Performers, orchestras and choirs. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Classical Album.

### Folk Traditions (42)

- [Mestre Bimba](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mestre-bimba.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1932 · tier S (Legend). Capoeira. Creator of capoeira regional; berimbau rhythms and ladainhas.
- [Teixeirinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/teixeirinha.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1959 · tier S (Legend). Gaúcho / nativist music. The "Gaúcho Coração do Rio Grande": "Coração de Luto" sold millions.
- [Boi Caprichoso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/boi-caprichoso.html): Collective · Amazonas · debut 1913 · tier A (Giant). Bumba-meu-boi and boi-bumbá. The blue bull of the Parintins Festival.
- [Boi Garantido](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/boi-garantido.html): Collective · Amazonas · debut 1913 · tier A (Giant). Bumba-meu-boi and boi-bumbá. The red bull of the Parintins Festival.
- [Lamartine Babo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/lamartine-babo.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1925 · tier A (Giant). Carnival marchinhas. "O Teu Cabelo Não Nega", the Flamengo anthem and those of other Rio clubs.
- [Braguinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/braguinha.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1929 · tier A (Giant). Carnival marchinhas. João de Barro: "Chiquita Bacana", "Yes, Nós Temos Bananas", "Touradas em Madri".
- [Capiba](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/capiba.html): Solo · Pernambuco · debut 1930 · tier A (Giant). Frevo. Composer of frevo-canção: "Madeira Que Cupim Não Rói".
- [Emilinha Borba](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/emilinha-borba.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1939 · tier A (Giant). Carnival marchinhas. Queen of radio and carnival marches, with "Chiquita Bacana".
- [Mestre Pastinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mestre-pastinha.html): Solo · Bahia · debut 1941 · tier A (Giant). Capoeira. Guardian of capoeira angola.
- [Lia de Itamaracá](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/lia-de-itamaraca.html): Solo · Pernambuco · debut 1960 · tier A (Giant). Coco and ciranda. The queen of ciranda, from Itamaracá.
- [Gaúcho da Fronteira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/gaucho-da-fronteira.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1970 · tier A (Giant). Gaúcho / nativist music. Vanerões and fandangos: "Bugio Fronteiriço".
- [Renato Borghetti](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/renato-borghetti.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1984 · tier A (Giant). Gaúcho / nativist music, Brazilian jazz, Chamamé. Button accordion that took gaúcho music to the world.
- [Tchê Garotos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tche-garotos.html): Band · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1992 · tier A (Giant). Tchê music. "Tchê music": 1990s pop vanerão.
- [Carrapicho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/carrapicho.html): Band · Amazonas · debut 1996 · tier A (Giant). Bumba-meu-boi and boi-bumbá. Manaus band of "Tic, Tic, Tac", a worldwide boi-bumbá hit.
- [Patativa do Assaré](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/patativa-do-assare.html): Solo · Ceará · tier A (Giant). Repente and cantoria. A folk poet and singer; author of "A Triste Partida", recorded by Luiz Gonzaga.
- [Maracatu Nação Leão Coroado](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/maracatu-nacao-leao-coroado.html): Collective · Pernambuco · debut 1863 · tier B (Reference). Maracatu. The oldest nação still active.
- [Maracatu Nação Estrela Brilhante](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/maracatu-nacao-estrela-brilhante.html): Collective · Pernambuco · debut 1906 · tier B (Reference). Maracatu. A Recife maracatu nação, living heritage.
- [Nelson Ferreira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/nelson-ferreira.html): Solo · Pernambuco · debut 1920 · tier B (Reference). Frevo. "Evocação nº 1".
- [Aurora Miranda](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/aurora-miranda.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1933 · tier B (Reference). Carnival marchinhas. Carmen Miranda's sister; made her record debut in 1933 with "Cai, Cai, Balão", alongside Francisco Alves.
- [Marlene](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/marlene.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1940 · tier B (Reference). Carnival marchinhas. Emilinha's rival in the Rádio Nacional auditoriums.
- [Mestre Salustiano](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mestre-salustiano.html): Solo · Pernambuco · debut 1950 · tier B (Reference). Maracatu, Repente and cantoria. Rabeca player and master of rural maracatu.
- [Caju & Castanha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/caju-e-castanha.html): Duo · Pernambuco · debut 1970 · tier B (Reference). Coco and ciranda, Repente and cantoria. Embolada and humour.
- [Os Serranos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/os-serranos.html): Band · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1970 · tier B (Reference). Gaúcho / nativist music. Gaúcho dance-hall music for decades.
- [Papete](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/papete.html): Solo · Maranhão · debut 1975 · tier B (Reference). Bumba-meu-boi and boi-bumbá. Percussion and bumba-meu-boi from Maranhão: "Bandeira de Aço".
- [Baitaca](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/baitaca.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1990 · tier B (Reference). Gaúcho / nativist music. Fandango and trova.
- [Luiz Marenco](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/luiz-marenco.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1990 · tier B (Reference). Gaúcho / nativist music. Contemporary nativist song.
- [Selma do Coco](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/selma-do-coco.html): Solo · Pernambuco · debut 1990 · tier B (Reference). Coco and ciranda. Coco de roda from Olinda.
- [Tchê Guri](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tche-guri.html): Band · debut 1990 · tier B (Reference). Tchê music. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Roots Album.
- [Lenine & Suzano](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/lenine-e-suzano.html): Duo · Pernambuco · debut 1993 · tier B (Reference). Frevo. "Olho de Peixe" (1993), guitar and percussion.
- [Flor Ribeirinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/flor-ribeirinha.html): Group · Mato Grosso · debut 1995 · tier B (Reference). Siriri and cururu. Siriri and cururu group from the São Gonçalo Beira Rio community in Cuiabá, a winner at folklore festivals around the world.
- [Tchê Barbaridade](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/tche-barbaridade.html): Band · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1996 · tier B (Reference). Tchê music. Tchê music.
- [César Oliveira & Rogério Melo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/cesar-oliveira-e-rogerio-melo.html): Duo · debut 1999 · tier B (Reference). Gaúcho / nativist music. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Roots Album.
- [Spok Frevo Orquestra](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/spok-frevo-orquestra.html): Band · Pernambuco · debut 2001 · tier B (Reference). Frevo, Brazilian jazz. Instrumental frevo with a jazz vocabulary.
- [André Filho](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/andre-filho.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Carnival marchinhas. Author of "Cidade Maravilhosa" (1935), Rio's anthem.
- [Carlos Galhardo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/carlos-galhardo.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Carnival marchinhas, Samba-canção. Radio-era singer of "Allah-lá-ô".
- [Chico da Silva](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/chico-da-silva.html): Solo · Amazonas · tier B (Reference). Bumba-meu-boi and boi-bumbá, Roots samba. A songwriter from Parintins, of boi toadas and sambas such as "Pandeiro É Meu Nome".
- [Jararaca](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jararaca.html): Solo · Alagoas · tier B (Reference). Carnival marchinhas. Co-writer of "Mamãe Eu Quero" (1937), of the duo Jararaca e Ratinho.
- [Jongo da Serrinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/jongo-da-serrinha.html): Group · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Jongo. Group from the Serrinha hill in Madureira that keeps jongo alive in Rio.
- [Mandicuera](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mandicuera.html): Collective · Paraná · tier B (Reference). Caiçara fandango. Caiçara culture association on Ilha dos Valadares, Paranaguá, which runs the National Caiçara Fandango Festival.
- [Mateus Aleluia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mateus-aleluia.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). Afro-Brazilian chants. Former member of Os Tincoãs who sings the Bantu and Yoruba heritage of the Recôncavo.
- [Os Tincoãs](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/os-tincoas.html): Group · Bahia · tier B (Reference). Afro-Brazilian chants. Bahian trio that brought candomblé chants into song in the 1970s; Mateus Aleluia came from it.
- [Vitor Ramil](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/vitor-ramil.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · tier B (Reference). Gaúcho / nativist music. A singer and writer from Pelotas, creator of the "aesthetics of the cold".

### Indigenous Music (6)

- [Marlui Miranda](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/marlui-miranda.html): Solo · tier A (Giant). Traditional songs. Singer and researcher of Indigenous music, of "2 IHU – Kewere: Rezar" (1997).
- [Brô MC's](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bro-mc-s.html): Group · Mato Grosso do Sul · debut 2009 · tier B (Reference). Contemporary Indigenous artists, Rap nacional. Guarani Kaiowá rap group from Dourados, rhyming in Guarani and Portuguese.
- [Djuena Tikuna](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/djuena-tikuna.html): Solo · Amazonas · tier B (Reference). Contemporary Indigenous artists. Singer of the Tikuna people who sings in her people's language.
- [Katú Mirim](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/katu-mirim.html): MC · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Contemporary Indigenous artists, Rap nacional. An Indigenous singer and rapper from Jundiaí.
- [Kaê Guajajara](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/kae-guajajara.html): Solo · tier B (Reference). Contemporary Indigenous artists. Singer-songwriter of the Guajajara people.
- [Owerá](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/owera.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Contemporary Indigenous artists, Rap nacional. Guarani Mbya rapper from São Paulo, formerly known as Kunumí MC.

### Children's Music (24)

- [A Turma do Balão Mágico](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/a-turma-do-balao-magico.html): Group · São Paulo · debut 1982 · tier S (Legend). Children's. "Superfantástico", "Amigos do Peito".
- [Xuxa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/xuxa.html): Solo · Rio Grande do Sul · debut 1986 · tier S (Legend). Children's. The "Queen of the Little Ones": "Ilariê"; the best-selling children's records in the country's history.
- [Galinha Pintadinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/galinha-pintadinha.html): Collective · São Paulo · debut 2006 · tier S (Legend). Children's. One of the most-watched children's channels on YouTube worldwide.
- [Patati Patatá](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/patati-patata.html): Duo · São Paulo · debut 1983 · tier A (Giant). Children's. Clown duo; records and sold-out tours.
- [Paquitas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/paquitas.html): Group · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1984 · tier A (Giant). Children's. Xuxa's stage assistants who became a children's phenomenon.
- [Trem da Alegria](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/trem-da-alegria.html): Group · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1984 · tier A (Giant). Children's. "Piuí Abacaxi", "Uni Duni Tê".
- [Hélio Ziskind](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/helio-ziskind.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1994 · tier A (Giant). Children's. Soundtracks for "Castelo Rá-Tim-Bum" and "Cocoricó".
- [Palavra Cantada](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/palavra-cantada.html): Duo · São Paulo · debut 1994 · tier A (Giant). Children's. Sandra Peres and Paulo Tatit: quality children's music; "Pindorama".
- [Mundo Bita](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mundo-bita.html): Collective · Pernambuco · debut 2011 · tier A (Giant). Children's. Musical animations with billions of views.
- [Os Saltimbancos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/os-saltimbancos.html): Collective · debut 1977 · tier B (Reference). Children's. Chico Buarque's version of the Italian musical, a children's classic.
- [A Patotinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/a-patotinha.html): Group · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1978 · tier B (Reference). Children's. "Natal Numa Discotheque", "Melô dos Patins".
- [Angélica](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/angelica.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · debut 1988 · tier B (Reference). Children's. "Vou de Táxi".
- [Eliana](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/eliana.html): Solo · São Paulo · debut 1993 · tier B (Reference). Children's. "Os Dedinhos".
- [Banda de Boca](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/banda-de-boca.html): Group · tier B (Reference). Children's. Nominated for the Latin Grammy for Best Children's Music Album.
- [Barbatuques](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/barbatuques.html): Group · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Children's. São Paulo body-percussion group.
- [Bia Bedran](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bia-bedran.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Children's. Singer and storyteller for children.
- [Bob Zoom](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/bob-zoom.html): Collective · tier B (Reference). Children's. A children's music channel.
- [Carequinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/carequinha.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Children's. Clown and singer of 1950s TV.
- [Grupo Triii](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/grupo-triii.html): Group · tier B (Reference). Children's. A children's music group.
- [Luccas Neto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/luccas-neto.html): Solo · Rio de Janeiro · tier B (Reference). Children's. Children's content creator and singer.
- [Mara Maravilha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/mara-maravilha.html): Solo · Bahia · tier B (Reference). Children's. Children's TV host and singer of the 1980s and 1990s.
- [Maria Clara & JP](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/maria-clara-e-jp.html): Duo · tier B (Reference). Children's. Siblings who are a hit on children's YouTube.
- [Pequeno Cidadão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/pequeno-cidadao.html): Band · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Children's. A children's music band made up of musicians and their kids.
- [Simony](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/artists/simony.html): Solo · São Paulo · tier B (Reference). Children's. Former member of A Turma do Balão Mágico.

## Singers (1071)

- [Elis Regina](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/elis-regina.html): The "Pimentinha", regarded as MPB's greatest interpreter: "Como Nossos Pais", "Águas de Março".
- [Milton Nascimento](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/milton-nascimento.html): A unique falsetto and timbre; Clube da Esquina and "Travessia".
- [Gal Costa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/gal-costa.html): The voice of Tropicália, from "Baby" to "Chuva de Prata".
- [Tim Maia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/tim-maia.html): The "Síndico", the voice of Brazilian soul.
- [Ney Matogrosso](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/ney-matogrosso.html): The countertenor of Secos & Molhados and of the country's most theatrical solo career.
- [Elza Soares](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/elza-soares.html): A husky voice and scat, from samba to the experimental; named singer of the millennium by the BBC in 1999.
- [Maria Bethânia](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/maria-bethania.html): A dramatic interpreter; the first Brazilian woman singer to pass a million records, with "Álibi".
- [Cássia Eller](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/cassia-eller.html): The deep voice of 1990s rock and MPB.
- [Marisa Monte](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/marisa-monte.html): The great MPB voice of the 1990s and 2000s; Tribalistas.
- [Renato Russo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/renato-russo.html): Legião Urbana's singer and lyricist.
- [Ivete Sangalo](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/ivete-sangalo.html): Axé's biggest star, from Banda Eva to her solo career.
- [Andre Matos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/andre-matos.html): Singer of Viper, Angra and Shaman; a reference in melodic metal.
- [Cazuza](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/cazuza.html): Voice and lyrics of Barão Vermelho and a solo career: "Exagerado", "Ideologia", "O Tempo Não Para".
- [Chorão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/chorao.html): Singer and lyricist of Charlie Brown Jr., the voice of 1990s and 2000s skate rock.
- [Marília Mendonça](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/marilia-mendonca.html): The "queen of sofrência", the voice of feminejo: "Infiel", "Todos os Cantos".
- [João Gilberto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/joao-gilberto.html): The minimal, whispered voice that defined bossa nova.

## Instrumentalists

### Guitarists (130)

- [Edu Ardanuy](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/edu-ardanuy.html): Dr. Sin; precise hard rock and heavy metal technique, author of the instrumental album "Electric Nightmare" (1998)
- [Mateus Asato](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/mateus-asato.html): From Campo Grande (MS); played with Jessie J, Tori Kelly and Bruno Mars and won the world through Instagram
- [Kiko Loureiro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/kiko-loureiro.html): Angra and Megadeth; a world-metal reference, author of the solo album "No Gravity"
- [Andreas Kisser](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/andreas-kisser.html): Sepultura; "Arise", "Chaos A.D." and "Roots"
- [Juninho Afram](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/juninho-afram.html): Oficina G3; the reference for Christian guitar and gospel rock
- [Mozart Mello](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/mozart-mello.html): Teacher who trained generations, including Edu Ardanuy and Kiko Loureiro
- [Pepeu Gomes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/pepeu-gomes.html): Novos Baianos; psychedelia with Brazilian rhythms, cited by Guitar World in the 1970s
- [Prika Amaral](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/prika-amaral.html): Nervosa; a female reference in thrash and extreme metal
- [Cacau Santos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/cacau-santos.html): Gospel guitar blending rock, jazz and Brazilian music
- [Luciano Carlos Cunha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/luciano-carlos-cunha.html): Composer, guitarist and music teacher in Florianópolis. A prolific guitarist and shredder, he moves across progressive rock, fusion, neoclassical metal, choro, suites, symphonic concertos and classical music.
- [Ximbinha](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/ximbinha.html): Banda Calypso; the guitar of Pará's brega

### Acoustic guitar and viola (19)

- [Baden Powell](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/baden-powell.html): Guitarist of the Afro-Sambas and "Canto de Ossanha".
- [Raphael Rabello](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/raphael-rabello.html): A virtuoso of the seven-string guitar.
- [Yamandu Costa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/yamandu-costa.html): Gaúcho seven-string guitarist, from choro to milonga.
- [Garoto](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/garoto.html): Aníbal Augusto Sardinha, a guitarist who anticipated bossa nova harmony.
- [Almir Sater](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/almir-sater.html): Viola player from Mato Grosso do Sul, a master of the viola caipira.
- [Tião Carreiro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/tiao-carreiro.html): The "king of the viola pagode", of the duo with Pardinho.
- [Dilermando Reis](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/dilermando-reis.html): Radio-era guitarist, a performer of waltzes and choros.
- [Paulinho Nogueira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/paulinho-nogueira.html): Guitarist and teacher, creator of the craviola.
- [Marco Pereira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/marco-pereira.html): Guitarist and arranger.
- [Turíbio Santos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/turibio-santos.html): Classical guitarist, a performer of Villa-Lobos.
- [Renato Andrade](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/renato-andrade.html): Minas Gerais player of instrumental viola caipira.
- [Roberto Corrêa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/roberto-correa.html): Viola player and researcher of the viola caipira.
- [Guinga](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/guinga.html): Rio guitarist and composer.
- [Paulo Bellinati](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/paulo-bellinati.html): São Paulo guitarist and composer.
- [Badi Assad](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/badi-assad.html): Guitarist and singer.
- [Sérgio Assad](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/sergio-assad.html): Guitarist of Duo Assad.
- [Odair Assad](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/odair-assad.html): Guitarist of Duo Assad.
- [João Pernambuco](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/joao-pernambuco.html): Guitarist and composer from the early days of Brazilian guitar.
- [Dino 7 Cordas](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/dino-7-cordas.html): Seven-string guitarist of Época de Ouro.

### Percussion (7)

- [Naná Vasconcelos](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/nana-vasconcelos.html): Recife berimbau percussionist, acclaimed in world jazz.
- [Airto Moreira](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/airto-moreira.html): Percussionist who took Brazilian percussion into jazz-fusion.
- [Marcos Suzano](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/marcos-suzano.html): Pandeiro player who renewed the instrument's language.
- [Carlinhos Brown](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/carlinhos-brown.html): Percussionist and creator of Timbalada.
- [Djalma Corrêa](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/djalma-correa.html): Bahian percussionist.
- [Dom Um Romão](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/dom-um-romao.html): Samba-jazz drummer and percussionist.
- [Jorginho do Pandeiro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/jorginho-do-pandeiro.html): Pandeiro player of Época de Ouro.

### Keyboards and piano (19)

- [João Donato](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/joao-donato.html): Pianist from Acre, a pioneer of bossa nova and Latin jazz.

- [Guiomar Novaes](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/guiomar-novaes.html): Classical pianist.

- [Ráae](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/raae.html)
- [Marco Mazzola](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/marco-mazzola.html): Producer of major MPB and rock albums since the 1970s.
- [Lincoln Olivetti](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/lincoln-olivetti.html): Arranger and producer of the 1980s pop sound.
- [Rogério Duprat](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/rogerio-duprat.html): Conductor and arranger of Tropicália.
- [Guto Graça Mello](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/guto-graca-mello.html): Producer and musical director at Som Livre.
- [Tom Capone](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/tom-capone.html): Producer of 1990s and 2000s rock.
- [Roberto Menescal](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/roberto-menescal.html): Producer and A&R director, one of the creators of bossa nova.
- [Arthur Verocai](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/arthur-verocai.html): Conductor and arranger of the cult 1972 album.
- [DJ Marlboro](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/dj-marlboro.html): Producer who gave funk carioca its Portuguese voice.
- [Eumir Deodato](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/eumir-deodato.html): Arranger and producer.
- [Nelson Motta](https://brazilianmusic.biblioverse.org/people/nelson-motta.html): Producer, songwriter and journalist.
